Authors: C.B., Huffaker, Carl B.
Title: Some ecological roots of pest control
Abstract: Development of pest management systems rests on relatively few major ecological principles and these underly the tactics and strategies available. Many are so self-evident that we often ignore their underlying significance. They are (1) the principle of inherent variation in the genetic properties of organisms; (2) the principle that an organism must be adapted to its environment and becomes so through its evolution; (3) the principle that all organisms require adequate nutrition; (4) the principle that to perpetuate their kind organisms must reproduce; (5) the principle that as organisms are born immature they must grow and develop; (6) the principle that life presents various compensations tending to correct for adverse occurrences; (7) the principle that most organisms derive their sustenance from other living organisms (predation); (8) the principle that organisms commonly suffer from depletion of resources by other organisms (competition among the same or different kinds of organisms); (9) the principle that cooperation serves many species well; (10) the principle that organisms must move about and do things (possess mobility and other behavior); and (11) the principle of holism and interactions among factors in ecosystems. Examples are given showing that advances in our knowledge in each of these basic areas are significant in developing ecologically sound pest management systems. © 1974 Le François. © 2007 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: H.W., Howard, H. W.
Title: Factors influencing the quality of ware potatoes. 1. The genotype
Abstract: Quality of ware potatoes is usually the result of genotype/environment interactions. It has many attributes including some, such as disease resistance and resistance to mechanical damage, that are not always considered when discussing quality. Potatoes for the various methods of cooking and for the several manufacturing processes may need to be of different types. From a nutritional point of view the potato is a very important source of vitamin C, and, although usually considered primarily as a source of carbohydrates (starch), the potato is important as a source of proteins. Little is known of varietal differences in content of vitamin C or in rates of loss on storage. There is a strong negative correlation between total yield and protein content, and, as in many other crops, the highest yield of protein per unit area is obtained from a high total yield and relatively low protein content. Potato protein is low in methionine, and it has been suggested that the level of this amino acid could be increased by breeding programmes. In most countries the most acceptable shape is the long oval; eyes should be shallow. For most purposes medium sized tubers of a uniform size are desirable. Shape and depth of eye are determined mainly by the genotype; size and number of tuber show genotype/environment interactions. Under certain conditions disease resistance is an integral part of good quality. Of particular importance may be spraing caused by the nematode-transmitted tobacco rattle virus and common scab (Streptomyces scabies). Varietal resistance to both diseases occurs. An absence of mechanical damage to tubers may be as important as any attribute in determining good quality. Although there may be varietal differences for susceptibility to damage, there are very big differences between harvests depending upon both soil and weather conditions. The avoidance of superficial damage ('scuffing') depends to a certain extent on the tubers being fully mature when harvested; it is thus partly determined by genotype. Deep damage ('bruising'), both at harvest and when sorting after storage, is often closely correlated with dry matter content-the higher the dry matter, the more susceptible to bruising and 'blue spot'. Varieties differ greatly in the dormancy of tubers and rate of sprouting, and hence in their keeping quality. The cooking quality of table potatoes can be considered under four headings: texture, colour, after-cooking discolouration and flavour. Texture (disintegration, consistency, mealiness, dryness and structure) is mainly determined by genotype, but environmental factors do have some effects. The only published genetical work is on mealiness, and the results suggest a rather simple determination. Yellow flesh colour is dominant to white, but there are modifying genes for different degrees of yellowness. Discolouration of cooked tubers has been investigated by many workers; it is controlled by both genotype and environment. Flavour is very difficult to assess; on the whole differences between varieties are more important than differences between soils. Consumer preference has also to be taken into account when considering the cooking quality of table varieties. There may have been a change in preference-from mealy varieties to those that do not break-down easily, for example to Bintje in the Netherlands and to King Edward in England. There is some evidence that it is easier to replace a variety of indifferent cooking quality that one of good quality. Potatoes for processing are considered under four headings-canned new potatoes, chips (crisps in the UK), French fries (pommes frites), and dehydrated granules and powders. The main requisite of a potato for canning is that the tubers should not disintegrate when boiled, canned and stored; freedom from breakdown is a varietal character. Potatoes for the production of chips should have a high dry matter content and should not produce brown chips; the latter is largely determined by reducing sugar content. Both high dry matter and low reducing sugar contents are varietal characters, but environment is also important. Potatoes for French fries and dehydrated products should on the whole have characters similar to those required for chip manufacture. Discolouration of raw potato flesh is a result of enzymic oxidation of tyrosine in injured cells, and it has no connection with after-cooking discolouration which is related to chlorogenic acid content. Raw flesh discolouration is controlled both by the genetic differences between varieties and the interaction of genotype and environment. The starch percentage and starch yield of potatoes varies both with variety and environments. There are also differences between varieties in the compostion of the starch (amylose: amylopectin ratio; and phosphoric acid content). Nearly all the attributes of good quality have a high heritability, and it should therefore be possible for breeders to produce varieties of good quality, particularly as there is no reason why a good quality variety should not have as high a yield as one of moderate quality. The main reason why some, recently produced, high-yielding varieties possess only moderate quality is the very small chance of a variety having resistance to many diseases and pests, having all the characters necessary to produce a high yield, and having in addition the many attributes of good quality. © 1974 Kluwer Academic Publishers. © 2007 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: D.E., Pinnock, Dudley E.; J.E., Milstead, James E.; N.F., Coe, N. F.; R.J., Brand, Richard J.
Author full names: Pinnock, Dudley E. (6701444577); Milstead, James E. (6701660971); Coe, N. F. (16516106700); Brand, Richard J. (57223658240)
Title: The effectiveness of Bacillus thuringiensis formulations for the control of larvae of Schizura concinna on Cercis occidentalis trees in California
Abstract: Five commercial formulations of Bacillus thuringiensis (Berliner) were found to be effective for control of larvae of the red-humped caterpillar, Schizura concinna (Smith & Abbot), an important defoliator of broad-leaved trees in California. The formulations tested were Biotrol® BTB 183 25 W, Biotrol® XK, Dipel®, Thuricide® HPC, and Thuricide® 90TS 950T. As a result of these trials, B. thuringiensis replaced chemical insecticides for the control of this pest in 1970, and has provided effective control as part of an operational pest management programme for four years. © 1974 Le François. © 2007 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: P., DeBach, Paul; G., Gordh, Gordon
Title: A new species of Aphytis that attacks important armored scale insects
Abstract: Aphytis roseni spec. nov. is described and its affinities with other members of the genus indicated. The parasite was imported into Peru from Africa for control of the rufous scale, Selenaspidus articulatus (Morgan). In Peru, A. roseni is achieving substantial biological control. © 1974 Le François. © 2007 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.R., Quezada, J. R.
Title: Biological control of Aleurocanthus woglumi [Homoptera: Aleyrodidae] in El Salvador
Abstract: The citrus blackfly, Aleurocanthus woglumiAsh., was first observed in El Salvador in 1965. Its dispersal was followed during a three-year period (1969-1972) in which it infested most citrus orchards in the country. Indigenous natural enemies as the predators Delphastus sp. and Chrysopa sp., and the pathogenic fungus Aschersonia aleyrodisWeb. are unable to exert any economic control of the pest. The introduction of the parasite Prospaltella opulentaSilvestri from Mexico brought about the successful biological control of the pest. Life table studies carried out before and after introduction of the parasite helped to assess the value of P. opulenta as an effective natural enemy of the citrus blackfly. © 1974 Le François. © 2007 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M.N., Beg, M. N.; F.D., Bennett, Frederick D.
Author full names: Beg, M. N. (16515784200); Bennett, Frederick D. (7102983526)
Title: Plagiprospherysa trinitatis [Dipt.: Tachinidae], A parasite of Elasmopalpus lignosellus [Lep.: Phycitidae] in Trinidad, W. I.
Abstract: Increased damage to sugarcane by Elasmopalpus lignosellus associated with preharvest burning in Barbados, has prompted an investigation of its natural enemies in Trinidad. Three parasites Plagiprospherysa trinitatisThompson, Macrocentrus sp. and Agathis rubricinctusAshmead were reared. Laboratory techniques for breeding P. trinitatis as well as its host are described. Attempts to utilize related species for biological control are reviewed and the possibilities of utilizing p. trinitatis are discussed briefly. © 1974 Le François. © 2007 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A.J., Wapshere, Anthony J.
Title: Host specificity of phytophagous organisms and the evolutionary centres of plant genera or sub-genera
Abstract: Chondrilla juncea is an important weed in Australia. The morphology, ecology and chromosome number of species of the genus Chondrilla indicate that the generic centre of evolution is in southern. Bussia and that dispersal has occurred westwards, as far as western Europe, with a reduction in the number of Chondrilla species. The number of organisms specific to Chondrilla also increases as one approaches the generic centre of evolution. Therefore, to discover the greatest number of specific, biological control organisms for a weed, surveys should commence initially at its generic evolutionary centre. The application of this principle to genera of other important Australian weeds, namely to Echium which has two evolutionary centres and to Heliotropium which has a number of sub-generic evolutionary centres is discussed. © 1974 Le François. © 2007 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: G.B., Quistad, Gary B.; L.E., Staiger, Luana E.; D.A., Schooley, David A.
Author full names: Quistad, Gary B. (7004520480); Staiger, Luana E. (7003553802); Schooley, David A. (7006131829)
Title: Environmental degradation of the insect growth regulator methoprene(isopropyl(2E, 4E)-11-methoxy-3,7,11-trimethyl-2,4-dodecadienoate). I. Metabolism by alfalfa and rice
Source title: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
Abstract: The metabolic fate of isopropyl (2E,4E)-11-methoxy-3,7,11-trimethyl-2,4-dodecadienoate, a new insect growth regulator (common name, methoprene; trademark, Altosid), was studied in alfalfa and rice as a function of time. The major metabolic pathways involved ester hydrolysis, O-demethylation, and oxidative scission of the 4-ene double bond. The principal nonpolar metabolite was 7-methoxycitronellal which was isolated from vapors evolved from the plants. Chromatographic evidence strongly suggests the incorporation of radiolabel from the extensively degraded (2E)-[5-14C]methoprene molecule into carotenoids, chlorophylls, and other higher molecular weight plant constituents. Yields of primary metabolites were grossly inflated (10× too high) unless thin layer chromatography was accompanied by prior purification by gel permeation chromatography because much radioactivity was attributed to coeluting natural products. Rapid metabolism of methoprene to biologically innocuous derivatives was characteristic of both rice, and alfalfa. © 1974, American Chemical Society. Authors: S.L., Poe, S. L.
Title: Emergence of Keiferia lycopersicella [Lepidoptera: Gelechiidae], and Apanteles sp. [Hymenoptera: Braconidae] from pupae and soil treated with insect growth regulators
Abstract: Two insect growth regulators (IGR's), ZR-619 (ethylin-methoxy-3,7,11-trimethyl-(2E, 4E)-2,4-dodecadienethiolate), and ZR-777 (Prop-2 ynyl 3,7,11-trimethyl-(2E, 4E)-dodecadienoate) were tested for potential use against the tomato pinworm, Keiferia lycopersicella (Walsh.) The IGR's were applied to cocoons and to soil where cocoons were formed. Both IGR's, alone and in combination, suppressed pinworn adult emergence from 23 to 7% when applied direct but were ineffective when applied to the soil. All treatments of IGR's in both methods of application reduced emergence of the parasito Apanteles sp. to 0% from levels as high as 61%. Use of the IGR's in this situation resulted in greater harm to potential biological control agents than in benefit to pest control. © 1974 Le François. © 2007 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: S.G., Moore, Syd G.; J., Kalmakoff1, J.; J.A.R., Miles1, J. A R
Title: An iridescent virus and a rickettsia from the grass grub costelytra zealandica (Coleoptera: Scarabaeidae)
Abstract: Natural iridescent virus and rickettsia infections of Costelytra zealandica (White) and Odontria sp. indet. larvae were studied at a site in the upper Pareora Gorge scenic reserve, S. Canterbury. By sequentially sampling the site, it was found that neither the iridescent virus nor the rickettsiae appear to give rise to host mortalities that significantly alter the population density. Many larvae were found that appeared healthy, but carried inapparent iridescent virus infections. These diseases are not suitable for biological control of the grass grub. © 1974 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. © 2015 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: S.G., Moore, Syd G.; J., Kalmakoff, James; J.A.R., Miles, John A.R.
Author full names: Moore, Syd G. (7403536755); Kalmakoff, James (7004181999); Miles, John A.R. (7402882261)
Title: Virus diseases of porina (Wiseana spp.; lepidoptera: Hepialidae) *2. transmission trials
Abstract: Three occluded viruses isolated from Wiseana sp. indet. larvae were experimentally transmitted through Wiseana larvae under field conditions. Wiseana iridescent virus was not transmitted. The only reasonable estimates of dosage: mortality relationships were for the nucleopolyhedrosis virus: LD50 approx. 1.4 x 109 polyhedra per m2; LT50 approx. 250 days. Only lst-instar larvae appear to be infectable, and this may also apply to the entomopox and granulosis viruses. The evidence suggests that, under certain conditions, simultaneous applications of the nucleopolyhedrosis and granulosis viruses resulted in a considerable reduction of susceptibility of larvae to nucleopolyhedrosis which was accompanied by a complete absence of infection by granulosis. However, simultaneous applications of the nucleopolyhedrosis and the entomopox viruses enhanced larval susceptibility to entomopox virus infection. The nucleopolyhedrosis virus could be useful as a long-term biological control agent, and mass virus production in the field may make control economically viable. © 1974 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. © 2015 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Analytical determination of compound 1080 (sodium fluoroacetate) residues in biological materials

The sample is degraded by oxygen combustion, and the liberated inorganic fluoride determined by an ion-specific electrode. Authors: D., Lessmann, Dietrich
Title: Zum Vorkommen von Megastigmus‐Arten und weiteren Samenschädlingen in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland
Abstract: On the distribution of seed pests in the Federal Republic of Germany. In the seeds of Juniperus communis and Sorbus aucuparia respectively Megastigmus bipunctatus Swed. and M. brevicaudis Ratz. were found for the first time in West Germany. Moreover M. aculeatus Swed. emerged from Rosa canina seeds, M. seitneri Hoff. from Larix seeds, M. spermotrophus Wachtl from Pseudotsuga menziesii seeds and M. suspectus Borr. from Abies alba and A. nordmanniana seeds. M. atedius Walk. was found living in the seeds of Picea orientalis, until now unknown as a host tree to Megastigmus. M. atedius was also found in Pinus strobus and in one case in Picea abies seeds. Habrocytus chrysos Walk. gave the first indication of the occurrence of parasites on M. spermotrophus in Germany. Further results relate to the emerging of M. bipunctatus and M. brevicaudis as well as the diapause of M. spermotrophus. Contrary to past reports it was proven that an emergence period of at least 4 years is possible. Other seed destroying insects found were Syntomaspis varians Walk., S. druparum Boh., Torymus azureus Boh., T. druparum Boh. and Tetrastichus strobilanae Ratz. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A., Daftari, A.
Title: Studies on rearing and bioecology of Eurygaster integriceps Put. (Hemiptera, Pentatomidae)
Abstract: Feeding with green wheat and moist wheat grains under laboratory conditions (27° C and 60 % relative humidity), several consecutive generations of Sunn pests (E. integriceps) have been produced. A comparison between those pests which migrated to the mountain ranges and those that were reared under the laboratory conditions indicated that the migrating flight did not have any significant effect on the fertility and number of eggs laid by females. The results of another comparison made between a group of Sunn pest reared on the host plant of Artemisia santanicum and a group reared without this plant also indicated that the host plant did not effect the fertility of the female. Both groups were able to mate and lay eggs. So the host plant of Artemisia santanicum may just have been used in the mountains as a shelter for the migrating pests. Über die Massenzucht und Bioökologie von Eurygaster integriceps Put. (Hemiptera, Pentatomidae) Bei Fütterung mit Weizenkeimlingen und ‐Körnern im Labor konnten mehrere Generationen der Getreidewanze E. integriceps in großer Individuenzahl erzielt werden. Beim Vergleich zwischen Labortieren und solchen Wanzen, die im Freiland regelmäßig im Sommer von den Tieflagen in das Bergland wandern, zeigte sich kein spezifischer Einfluß der Wanderung auf die Fruchtbarkeit und Eizahl. Die ins Bergland gewanderten Tiere waren dort imstande, sich auf dem Unkraut Artemisia santanicum zu entwickeln. Diese Pflanze dient somit dem Schädling als Fraßrefugium. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: H.S., Salama, Hussien S.; M.K., Hamdy, Magdy K.
Author full names: Salama, Hussien S. (7004424583); Hamdy, Magdy K. (7006251856)
Title: Studies on populations on two scale insects infesting fig trees in Egypt (Coccoidea)
Abstract: Asterolecanium pustulans Ckll. and Hemiberlesia lataniae (Sign.) are major pests of fig trees in Burg El‐Arab. The former species had an annual peak of abundance in October and passed through three annual generations. The optimum temperature for its development ranged between 23–25.3° C. The latter species had a peak of abundance in September and passed through two annual generations. The favourable temperature for its development ranged between 25.3–26° C. Über Populationsbewegungen zweier Schildlausarten an Feigenbäumen in Ägypten Asterolecanium pustulans Ckll. und Hemiberlesia lataniae (Sign.) sind wichtige Schädlinge der Feigenbäume im Gebiet von Burh El‐Arab. Die erstgenannte Art erreichte ihre größte Dichte im Oktober und durchlief 3 Generationen im Jahr. Ihre optimalen Temperaturbedingungen lagen zwischen 23 und 25,3° C. Die zweitgenannte Art hatte ihre Populationsspitze bereits im September und vollendete nur 2 Generationen jährlich. Ihre optimale Temperatur lag höher zwischen 25,3 und 26° C. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: E., Graf, E.
Title: Zur Biologie und Gradologie des Grauen Lärchenwicklers, von Zeiraphera diniana Gn. (Lep., Tortricidae), im schweizerischen Mittelland: Teil 2 Lebenstafel und Ausbreitung
Abstract: Studies on the bionomy and gradology of the grey larch Tortricid, Zeiraphera diniana Gn. in Middle Suisse. Part 2: Life tables and origin of the moths of the second generation. The most important regulating factors were a. animals predating eggs and larvae, b. insufficient adaptation of the larvae to food and climate as well as of the prepupae and pupae to soil. The index of propagation during 3 generations amounted to about 0.7. For this the population of Z. diniana in Middle Suisse can exist only by immigration of moths of the second generation from the areals southern and southwestern which are optimal for the pest. Der Lärchenwickler, Zeiraphera diniana Gn., bevölkert nicht nur die subalpinen Lärchen‐Arven‐Mischwälder, wo er zwischen 1600–2000 m ü. M. zyklische Massenvermehrungen durchläuft, sondern ist auch latent im schweizerischen Mittelland vorhanden. In ersten Un‐tersuchungen wurde versucht, vor allem die Phaenologie und die Lebenstafel der latenten Population in Lenzburg (Kanton Aargau) etwas zu erhellen. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.A., Rudinsky, Julius A.; M.E., Morgan, Max E.; L.M., Libbey, Leonard M.; T.B., Putnam, Teryl B.
Author full names: Rudinsky, Julius A. (6506552772); Morgan, Max E. (7403025596); Libbey, Leonard M. (7003742767); Putnam, Teryl B. (7003309894)
Title: Additional components of the Douglas fir beetle (Col., Scolytidae) aggregative pheromone and their possible utility in pest control
Abstract: The identity of a reported Dendroctonus pseudotsugae attractant, 3‐methyl‐2‐cyclohexen‐1‐ol (MCH‐ol), was confirmed by GLC/MS analysis of volatiles collected over live attractive female. In bioassay with previously known attractants, MCH‐ol synergistically evoked male arrestment and stridulation in the laboraotry and high attraction predominantly of males in the field. Verbenone was similarly identified and was synergistically active to a lesser degree. The known double effect of the antiaggragetive pheromone 3‐methyl‐2‐cyclohexen‐1‐one (MCH) was confirmed, at it repressed response to the attractants at high concentration but at very low concentration it increased response to MCH‐ol and frontalin. The highest field response occurred to these three components together. Comparative GLC of feces and volatiles from pairs supports the belief that fecal release of MCH with the other attractants is quantitatively less than the release stimulated by the presence of the male and/or its sonic signal. Weitere Komponenten des Aggregations‐Pheromons von Dendroctonus pseudotsugae (Col., Scolyt.) Aus den Duftstoffen lebender Käfer von Dendroctonus pseudotsugae wurde 3‐methyl‐2‐cyclohexen‐1‐ol (MCH‐ol) gewonnen und seine Identität chromatographisch sowie auch massenspektrometrisch bestätigt. In Laborversuchen bewirkte MCH‐ol, in Verbindung mit den schon bekannten Pheromonen, eine stark zunehmende Anlockung sowie Stridulation der Männchen. Auch in Freilandversuchen lockte dieses Pheromon die fliegenden Borkenkäfer, vor allem die Männchen, stark an. Als weiteres Pheromon wurde Verbenone aus den lebenden Borkenkäfern gewonnen, doch war es synergistisch weniger aktiv. Die bekannte Doppelwirkung des antiaggregativen Pheromons 3‐methyl‐2‐cyclohexen‐1‐one (MCH) wurde bestätigt: eine höhere Konzentration des MCH blockierte die Anlockung an die attraktiven Stoffe gänzlich, während es in sehr geringer Konzentration die Anlockung an Frontalin und MCH‐ol erheblich vergrößerte. Die größte Anlockung wurde im Felde erzielt, wenn die drei Pheromone zusammen angeboten wurden. Vergleichende chromatographische Untersuchungen des Borkenkäferfrasses, des Kotes und der Duftstoffe zeigten, daß die Freisetzung von MCH aus Borkenkäferkot quantitativ bedeutend geringer ist als die Freigabe, die durch die Anwesenheit des Männchens und seine Stridulation stimuliert wird. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A.S., Srivastava, A. S.; K.M., Srivastava, K. M.; R.P., Singh, R. P.
Title: Effect of different dates of sowing of pea (Pisum sativum L.) on the yield and incidence of Phytomyza atricornis M. (pea leaf miner) and Etiella zinkenella Tr. (pea pod borer)
Abstract: The infestation of two pests, pea leaf miner and pea pod borer was studied in relation to varying dates of sowing in pea crop. It was found that the incidence of pea leaf miner was decreasing with the late sowing of pea crop, while the infestation of pea pod borer was increasing during the same period. The yield is inversely related with the incidence of Phytomyza atricornis M. but directly related with that of Etiella zinkenella Tr. The atmospheric temperature is directly related with the incidence of pea pod borer. 20th October is a very suitable date for sowing pea crop for the least pest incidence. Title: Insecticidal and Acaricidal Activity of Certain O,O-Dialkyl O-3-Pyridazinyl Phosphorothioates
Abstract: Forty-three 3-pyridazinyl phosphorothioates were evaluated for insecticidal and acaricidal activities against two-spotted spider mite, turnip aphid, smaller brown planthopper, mosquito larvae and American cockroach. Approximate acute oral toxicity of these compounds in mice was also examined. In general, the toxicity in mice was in parallel with the pesticidal activity, but a few compounds clearly showed a high degree of selectivity between pests and mice. Especially O,O-dimethyl O-(6-cyclohexyloxy-3-pyridazinyl) phosphorothioate showed substantially reduced mammalian toxicity but maintained high insecticidal and acaricidal activity. © 1974, Japan Society for Bioscience, Biotechnology, and Agrochemistry. Authors: D., Schröder, Dieter
Title: Untersuchungen über die Aussichten einer biologischen Bekämpfung von Scolytiden an Ulmen als Mittel zur Einschränkung des „Ulmensterbens”
Abstract: Studies on the possibilities of biological control of elm bark beetles (Scolytidae) with the view of reduction of the dutch elm disease. At the request of the Michigan State University the parasite complex of the European elm bark beetles, S. scolytus and S. multistriatus, was studied in eastern Austria by the European Station, C.I.B.C., in 1969. 10 species of parasites, the Braconids Coeloides scolyticida, Dendrosoter protuberans, Ecphylus silesiacus and Spathius rubidus, and the Chalcids Cheiropachus quadrum, Cerocephala cornigera, Dinotiscus aponius, Entodon ergias, Eurytoma arctica, and Eurytoma morio were found. Between 1970 and 1972 the studies were continued on behalf of the Canadian Forestry Service, and the mortality of the summer generation of S. scolytus and S. multistriatus was studied in two localities in 1970 and 1971. The total mortality between June and September was 76,3 and 79,3% for S. scolytus, and 75,1 and 84,8% for S. multistriatus. The mortality of the eggs (between 16 and 25%) was mainly caused by physical factors, losses through predation remained below 2,5%. The mortality of the first and second instar larvae reached 48% for S. scolytus, and 64% for S. multistriatus. Between 6 and 25% of the mortality of these two instars was caused by predation, the Dolichopodid M. nitida being the most important predator. The mortality of the larval instars L<inf>3–5</inf> accounted for 30% of the total mortality. Seven species of ectoparasites were responsible for most of this mortality. C. coeloides was the most important parasite of S. scolytus, and D. protuberans was the dominant parasite of S. multistriatus. Parasitism by the endoparasite E. ergias remained below 5% in the larvae of both species. No mortality was observed for the pupae and the teneral adults. No diseased larvae or pupae were found. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M., Osada, Masaru; Y., Itô, Yosiaki
Title: Population dynamics of pieris rapae crucivora boisduval (lepidoptera: Pieridae), an introduced insect pest in okinawa
Source title: Japanese Journal of Applied Entomology and Zoology
Abstract: Life tables for winter-spring generations of Pieris rapae crucivora, which had been accidentally introduced into the island of Okinawa in 1958, showed the basically similar mortality pattern with the spring populations of this species in the mainland of Japan. Due to the rareness of an important larval parasite, Apanteles glomeratus, and the lack of a pupal parasite, Pteromalus puparum, and the granulosis virus, total generation mortality was so low that the population density could rapidly built up through spring. Mark-recapture analysis of the adult population gave mean adult duration of 1.6 days for February and 2.9 days for March. © 1974, JAPANESE SOCIETY OF APPLIED ENTOMOLOGY AND ZOOLOGY. Authors: I.M., Ipe, Ipe M.
Title: Morphological, behavioural and biological studies of Melanagromyza obtusa (Malloch) (Diptera: Agromyzidae) on Cajanus indicus Spreng
Abstract: This paper deals with the behaviour and biology of Melanagromyza obtusa (Malloch) a serious pest of Cajanus indicus Spreng, one of the staple pulse crops of Northern India. In addition to brief morphological descriptions of various instars a key for their identification is given. The incubation period has been found to vary between 51.9 to 60.0 hrs. Average duration of the 1st instar was found to be 37.3 hrs, while total larval duration was found to be 142.6 hrs. Pupal duration at controlled conditions (29°C and 86–90% RH) was 186.7 hrs while at normal laboratory conditions it was 224.4 hrs. Copulation was observed between 8.00 am and 4.00 pm, usually a day after emergence while a single pair copulated even after 30 days of emergence. Duration of copulation varied between 45 mts to 2 hrs 55 mts. 40.7% pods were infested during January while 12.2 % of seeds were infested during peak Studien zur Morphologie, Lebens‐ und Verhaltensweise von Melanagromyza obtusa (Malloch) (Dipt.: Agromyzidae) an Cajanus indicus Spreng Die Arbeit berichtet über die Samenfliege M. obtusa, einem bedeutenden Schädling der Haupthülsenfrucht Nordindiens, Cajanus indicus. Zunächst werden die äuβeren Merkmale der verschiedenen Entwicklungsstadien beschrieben und ein Schlüssel zu ihrer Bestimmung gegeben. Die Embryonal‐Entwicklung dauerte 52–60 Stunden. Die mittlere Entwicklungsdauer der Erstlarven betrug 37,3 Stunden, die gesamte Larvenzeit 142,6 Stunden. Authors: V., Delucchi, V.
Title: Die konventionelle biologische Bekämpfung — ein Stiefkind des Pflanzenschutzes
Abstract: Conventional biological control — a poor relative of plant protection. Mean's activity is a permanent source of disturbing factors affecting the relationship between populations at different trophic levels. Objective of biological control is not only the transfer of natural enemies into areas where an undesirable species has been introduced without them, but also the analysis of factors which may improve the efficiency of indigenous natural enemies. The disappearance of alternate hosts, or the elimination of important plants on which natural enemies feed, or the removal of refugees where natural enemies can aestivate or hibernate, may have disastrous consequences on the survival of beneficial organisms and be the main cause of plant protection problems. The modification of cultural practices which are deleterious to natural enemies can be in many cases envisaged without additional investments. The periodic colonization of parasitoids and predators has shown to be a valuable technique, but much remains to be done if stabilization of antagonistic populations has to be achieved at a tolerable level over an entire season. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: G.B., El-Saadany, G. B.
Title: A new light trap for controlling lepidopterous insect pests in Egypt
Abstract: A newly‐designed light‐trap fitted with electrocuting grids, gave evidence of being far superior to a regular type in catching lepidopterous moths. Some of the latters are predominantly injurious agricultural pests in Egypt, e. g., about 10 000 cotton leaf‐worm moths were captured, in the new trap, over a two weeks period in a semiagricultural area. This in itself is an indication of the possibility that such a trap could serve as a method for the physical controlling of such pests if used extensively and in cotton growing areas. With the rapid of electricity in the Egyptian country‐side, it could be possible to include this method in an integrated programme of, at least, the cotton leaf worm control. Eine neue Lichtfalle zur Bekämpfung schädlicher Insekten in Ägypten Es wurde eine neue, mit einem elektrisch geladenen Gitter versehene Lichtfalle zum Fang von Schmetterlingen in Ägypten konstruiert. Von einer Reihe landwirtschaftlich schädlicher Arten wurden mit der neuen Falle innerhalb von zwei Wochen rund 10 000 Individuen der Baumwollblatteule, Spodoptera littoralis, gefangen. Daraus ergibt sich, daß die Falle auch zur physikalischen Bekämpfung derartiger Schädlinge dienen kann. Im Zuge der Elektrifizierung der ägyptischen Landwirtschaft könnte diese Methode Bestandteil eines Programms zur integrierten Bekämpfung der Baumwollblatteule werden. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: I., Iglisch, Ingram
Title: Ein naturgemäßes Verfahren zur Bekämpfung von Stechmücken (Diptera: Culicidae)
Abstract: A natural method for controlling mosquitoes (Diptera, Culicidae). The application of “poisonous substances” in pest control means a measure contradicting natural conditions. However, the conversion of the natural environment into a human environment — a process which cannot be stopped — would also have to be counted under this heading unless it will be possible to recall, or develop intentionally, measures for landscape development, for shaping the human environment as such that eventually will not have destructive but rather constructive effect, i.e. that take effect within the context of life. This means that the living conditions of the pests concerned will have to be designed to be less favourable for them while a sound landscape structure is maintained. For all long time, drainage has been considered as one of the most elegant measures to resolve mosquito problems. Drainage can be formed, however, only in situations where, due to human interference, the groundwater level has not yet decreased to a critical degree. And where could we still afford a reduction beyond the present level? The life of mosquitoes is closely interrelated with water levels in their habitat. Together with the hydrologic conditions of a given region which in turn depend on climate, a superordinate entity is formed. In this case, control of a mass development of mosquitoes as a pest that does not affect the environment, is achieved by a corresponding adjustment of hydrologie conditions. A uniform water supply to mosquito breeding areas and maintenance of an approximately constant water level over the year will eliminate the risk of a mass development of mosquitoes of the genus Aëdes meaning pests at our geographical latitude, because flooding (which cannot take place any more) will be required for the eggs deposited at dry sites; otherwise, the larvae which are aquatic could not hatch. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: B., Hurpin, B.
Title: Perspectives et contraintes de la lutte microbiologique
Abstract: Prospects and problems of microbial control. In spite of the existence of hundreds of entomopathogenic germs, only a few commercialized preparations are available or may be used for practical application. These data outline the importance of researches in order to solve the various ecological, pathological, microbiological, technological, hygienic and economic problems before developing the production of a pathogen convenient for microbial control according to the integrated control conceptions. Among these problems, methods of application in the field, characteristics related to the virulence of the various strains of one pathogen and to its specificity, the difficulties found in the mass production, and the safety tests towards Vertebrates are discussed. A national and international cooperation is required between scientists, industries, technicians in pest control in order to investigate these various aspects and to obtain positive results as soon as possible. Aussichten und Grenzen der mikrobiologischen Insektenbekämpfung Obwohl mehrere hundert entomopathogene Krankheitserreger bekannt sind, verfügen wir heute nur über wenige im Handel erhältliche oder sonst nutzbare Präparate für Versuche in der Praxis. Dieser Zahlenvergleich zeigt die Bedeutung der Forschung, die sich bemüht, die verschiedensten Probleme zu lösen, die hierbei auftauchen: ökologische, pathologische, mikrobiologische, technologische, hygienische, wirtschaftliche, die sich alle vor der end‐gültigen Fertigstellung eines Handelsproduktes auf der Basis eines Pathogens stellen, das geeignet ist, bei der mikrobiologischen Bekämpfung gemäß Konzeption des integrierten Pflanzenschutzes angewandt zu werden. Unter den genannten Problemen werden hier besonders diskutiert, wie sich die Wirkung dieser Krankheitserreger im Freiland fördern läßt, die Kennzeichen, die mit der Virulenz der verschiedenen Stämme ein‐ und desselben Entomopathogens verbunden sind, die Spezi‐fität desselben, die dabei auftretenden Begrenzungen für die Massenproduktion und die Kontrollen der Unbedenklichkeit gegenüber Vertebraten. Um gemeinsam die verschiedenen Aspekte untersuchen und möglichst schnell zu konkreten Ergebnissen vorstoßen zu können, ist eine nationale und internationale Zusammenarbeit zwischen den Forschern, den Indu‐striefirmen und den Pflanzenärzten dringend notwendig. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.J.F.E., de Wilde, Jan J.F.E.
Title: Insektenhormone und Insektenbekämpfung
Abstract: Insect hormones and pest control. This paper deals with the effects of insect hormones and their bio‐analogues as possible tools in pest control. After a brief review of the natural regulators of insect growth, the Juvenile Hormone and the juvenoid mimetics are discussed in more detail. The nature of the induced disturbances of growth and reproduction, the relation between dosage and effect, selectivity, mammalian toxicity, resistance and secundary effects are treated in succession. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M., Sy, M.
Title: Anwendungsbereich und Leistung von Giftködern bei Hausschädlingen
Abstract: Efficacy and range of application of poison baits for controlling household insect pests. In practice, the control of some household insects turns out to be inadequate and insufficient, taking for example the Pharao ant (Monomorium pharaonis L.) and cockroaches. The reason for this is not the inadequacy of the insecticide used but mistakes in method which seem almost inevitable with laymen. Two very highly attractive poison baits have been developed especially for the species mentioned above. In field experiments — provided that all of the infested area was treated — total eradication of the ant population was achieved. If single buildings, surrounded by other infested buildings, were treated alone eradication of the Pharao ant was successful. If the baits were left in place, re‐infestation from the surrounding area was prevented, — whereas in the use of contact insecticides, re‐infestation is inevitable. In the case of cockroaches, too, eradication is achieved by the use of poison baits. Re‐invasion, however, is more likely with cockroaches, as they are continuously brought in together with all kinds of goods. Leaving the baits in place will keep re‐infestation to a minimum. There is hope that, in practice, the application of baits will offer greater chances of success, since this method is practically foolproof in its application as compared to contact insecticides. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J., Freuler, J.; P., Antonin, Ph; G., Raboud, G.; R., Veuthey, R.; R., Murbach, R.
Title: Vorbereitende Arbeiten zur Einführung des integrierten Pflanzenschutzes im Gemüsebau der Westschweiz
Abstract: Preparations for introduction of integrated pest control in market gardening in Western Switzerland. The appearence of tolerant or resistant pests, the changing of norms for the assessment of the quality of agricultural products, especially vegetables, the reduced number of pesticides available and the need, to make use of the separate areas of knowledge are the reasons to promote the idea of integrated pest control in market gardening. The trials in the canton of Valais with onions, carrots and tomatos have demonstrated the existence of the following problems: too many treatments, treatments against imaginary pests and the use of prescribed chemicals. An inventry of diseases and pests has been established and the influence on the production estimated. The experiments showed increased production for onions with insecticides and for carrots with fungicides but only marginally significant and not every season. For tomatos the necessity of at least 3 fungicides treatments has been established. Aphides are mainly treated to prevent the deposition of excretions which leave unsightly but not damaging spots on the produce. In future the main weight of the programme will be the elaboration of predictive techniques and development of methods to measure the economic tolerance threshold of the different insect pests. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: H., Wilbert, Hubert
Title: Die Ursachen von Fluktuation, Regulation und Determination bei Insektenpopulationen
Abstract: The causes of fluctuation, regulation and determination in insect populations. Well aimed measures against pest populations presuppose some knowledge of the causes of fluctuation, regulation and determination. All factors that affect fecundity, mortality, immigration or emigration are potential causes of fluctuations. Regulation comes about by factors that are negatively correlated with population density. They are often difficult to ascertain empirically because the correlation is influenced by additional variables. These variables may change it again and again by shifting the “set point” of the regulation. In this way, however, they are the main causes of determination: By their kind and range of variation they determine the limits as well as the temporal mean value of population density. If the regulating factors show “proportional behaviour”, permanent influences on the population can also be important for determination. Gezielte Eingriffe in Schädlingspopulationen verlangen Kenntnisse über die Ursachen von Fluktuation, Regulation und Determination. Potentielle Ursachen von Fluktuationen sind alle Faktoren, die Fruchtbarkeit, Sterblichkeit, Zu‐ und Abwanderung beeinflussen. Die Regulation kommt durch Faktoren zustande, die mit der Populationsdichte negativ korre‐liert sind. Ihr empirischer Nachweis wird erschwert durch äußere Einflüsse, welche die Kor‐relation immer wieder im Sinne von ”Sollwertverstellungen„ ändern und damit der un‐mittelbaren Beobachtung entziehen. Diese Einflüsse sind damit wesentliche Ursachen der Determination, indem sie über die erreichbaren Grenzen und den zeitlichen Mittelwert der Populationsdichte entscheiden. Soweit die regelnden Faktoren Proportionalverhalten zeigen, können auch permanente Einflüsse auf die Population selbst dabei Bedeutung haben. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M., Stengel, M.
Title: Integrierte Bekämpfung des Maiszünslers Ostrinia nubilalis Hübn. (Lepidopt. Pyralidae) im Elsaß
Abstract: Integrated control of the European corn borer, Ostrinia nubilalis (Hübn.) in Alsace. The European corn borer is a great corn pest. His borer activity is the origin of a yield loss reaching the half of the crop. La Pyrale du maĩs est un ravageur dangereux du ma˜s. Elle peut être la cause de chutes de rendement allant jusqu'à la moitié de la récolte. On peut lutter préventivement contre elle pa le hachage et l'enfouissement des résidus de récolte. On améliore aussi ainsi la structure et la teneur en matière humique du sol. L'utilisation de variétés résistantes ou tolérantes est une autre voie de contrôle. Lorsqu'en cours de végétation le seuil de tolérance de 10 à 12% de pieds avec une ponte est atteint on interviendra par lutte insecticide. Il faudra choisir de préférence un insecticide qui ne tue pas les parasites de la Pyrale. Les préparations à base de Bacillus thuringiensis ont cet avantage. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: E., Kangas, Esko
Title: Über die in der Orientierungsphase der Borkenkäfer auftretenden Prinzipien
Abstract: Principles involved in the orientation of bark beetles. The complete reproductive process of forest insect pests breeding (“gebunden lebenden”) in bark and phloem (e.g. bark beetles) can be divided into three phases: orientation, attack, and the breeding phase including the establishment of larval galleries. Successful orientation, i.e. the selection of suitable breeding material, is essential for the reproduction of these species. The orientation, which precedes attack on the breeding material, is based on the relations and reactions between the pest species and the tree. The principles involved in the orientation reactions of pests (e.g. changes in reaction phases, optimal level of stimuli, and the threshold principle) are described with examples. The orientation which precedes an attack does not always lead to successful development of a new generation (e.g. because of reactions of living breeding material). If, after successful orientation, a specimen of the population attacks the breeding material and by producing population pheromones attracts other specimens to the same material, this is to be considered part of the attack phase. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: N.K., Tiwari, N. K.
Title: Eurytoma nesiotes Crawford (Hym.: Chalcidoidea) an external parasite of gall midge Asphondylia sesami Felt
Abstract: Eurytoma nesiotes Crawford an ectoparasite of Asphondylia sesami Felt was reared and studied in the laboratory. Eggs are usually laid singly. Parasite remained externally on the body of the host throughout its development. Percentage of parasitism was quite high and the parasite can safely be utilized in the biological control projects. Eurytoma nesiotes Crawf. (Hym.: Chalcidoidea), ein Ektoparasit der Gallmücke Asphondylia sesami Felt. Als häufiger Parasit von A. sesami wurde Eurytoma nesiotes gezogen und näher untersucht. Die Eier wurden gewöhnlich einzeln abgelegt. Der Parasit bleibt während seiner Entwicklung außerhalb des Wirtskörpers. Die Parasitierung war zum Teil sehr hoch. Der Parasit ist geeignet, als Mittel zur biologischen Bekämpfung in Erwägung gezogen zu werden. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: H., Steiner, Hans
Title: Erfahrungen bei der Entwicklung und Einführung des integrierten Pflanzenschutzes in Baden‐Württemberg
Abstract: Experiences with the development and introduction of integrated control measures in Baden‐Württemberg. The first experiences with the integrated control were won in apple orchards. A fundamental inventory of the apple tree fauna was established and was followed by testing the influences of pesticides on the animals living there. On the course of the predatory work quantitative methods of the faunistical sampling were improved and accordingly the economic thresholds for the most important apple pests were ascertained. Data obtained have made possible the first field‐trials on large plots. It was found that this procedure does not function only, but also it works commercially with more benefits. Since there was no qualified advisory system, plant protection officers were trained; however, they have not enough time for that special task and no time at all for checking the orchards of interested farmers. That was the reason why the latter themselves have been trained. This is still to be considered as a model, since it is a question of 150 growers with a total area of about 650 hectares only. Results obtained till now are satisfactory. The state government is intending to expand the apple area with integrated control to about 5000 hectares. In the same area, preparatory investigations have started to develop integrated control for stone‐ and soft fruit cultures as well as for vegetable crops. Results obtained already show that integrated control is also possible for annual crops with normal plant rotation, if the area as a whole is considered and not only the crop species. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: H., Laven, Hannes
Title: Möglichkeiten der genetischen Schädlingsbekämpfung
Abstract: Possibilities of controlling insects by genetical methods. Up to this time only a few practical experiences are made in controlling insect pests by help of genetical methods. The differences between this method and the sterile male technique are shown and seven ways of genetic control are discussed. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: L., Brader, L.
Title: Zweck und Aufgaben integrierter Schädlingsbekämpfung
Abstract: Intention and problems of integrated pest control. As opposed to preventive chemical control integrated control intends to make a lasting and reliable plant protection possible. In such a system chances for the development of secundary pests and a building up of insecticide resistant strains are minimal. The emergency which arises when a totally resistant strain appears in cultures which have been sprayed frequently makes it necessary to reduce the amount of insecticide used. To introduce integrated control in practice several obstacles of a different nature have to be surmounted. For example the unacquaintedness of the farmer with this new control method and the necessity for intensive consultation. In only a few cultures research has been so far developed that a practical application is possible. From a purely biological‐technical point of view the chances for integrated control are exellent, but it is also clear that many prejudices have yet to be overcome. Im Gegensatz zur präventiven chemischen Bekämpfung will die integrierte Bekämpfung einen dauerhaften und zuverlässigeren Pflanzenschutz ermöglichen. In einem solchen System sind die Chancen der Entwicklung sekundärer Schadinsekten zu Hauptschädlingen und insektizidresistenter Stämme auf ein Minimum reduziert. Die Notlage beim Auftreten völlig resistenter Stämme in häufig gespritzten Kulturen macht es notwendig, den Insek‐tizidaufwand rechtzeitig zu reduzieren. Bei der Anwendung der integrierten Bekämpfung in der Praxis gibt es noch Hindernisse sehr verschiedener Art. Zum Beispiel die Unkenntnis dieser neuen Pflanzenschutzmethoden bei den Bauern und die Notwendigkeit einer inten‐siven Beratung. Die Untersuchungen sind erst in einigen Kulturen so weit entwickelt, daß eine praktische Anwendung möglich ist. Rein biologisch‐technisch gesehen, können die Aussichten der integrierten Bekämpfung bestimmt als gut bezeichnet werden, aber es ist auch sicher, daß nodi viele Vorurteile über‐wunden werden müssen. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: L., Bravenboer, Lubertus
Title: Entwicklungen bei der biologischen Bekämpfung in Gewächshäusern
Abstract: Problems in biological control of pests in glasshouses. The predating mite Phytoseiulus persimilis, introduced into glasshouses controlled spider mites on cucumbers successfully. The controlling of white flies especially on tomatoes and paprica, was made possible by help of the parasite Encarsia formosa. In consequence of the absence of wide spread pesticides several other pests, in particular Thripidae and Mites, increased. About this new studies are to be made. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: P., Starý, Petr
Title: Taxonomy, origin, distribution and host range of Aphidius species (Hym., Aphidiidae) in relation to biological control of the pea aphid in Europe and North America
Abstract: The parasite spectrum (Aphidius spp.) of Acyrthosiphon pisum is analysed and discussed with respect to its peculiarities in Europe and North America. The species are reviewed, specific criteria analysed and keys to identification added. Host range, relative abundance and interspecific relations are checked with respect to the existing opinions and author's own records. Recommendations for the release of some parasite species in Europe are given. Über Taxonomie, Herkunft, Verbreitung und Wirtskreis von Aphidius‐Arten (Hymen. Aphidiidae) in Beziehung zur biologischen Bekämpfung der Erbsenblattlaus in Europa und Nordamerika Das Parasitenspektrum (Aphidius ssp.) der Blattlaus Acyrthosiphon pisum wird analysiert und hinsichtlich seiner Besonderheiten in Europa und Nordamerika diskutiert. Eine kritische Übersicht über die Arten wird gegeben, Bestimmungsschlüssel werden aufgestellt. Der Wirtskreis, die relative Abundanz und die interspezifischen Beziehungen werden dargestellt im Hinblick auf die bisher bestehenden Meinungen sowie eigenen Ergebnisse. Es werden Empfehlungen für Freilassungen einiger Aphidius‐Arten in Europa als Mittel biologischer Schädlingsbekämpfung gegeben. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: H., Sandner, H.
Title: Die Richtungen in der gegenwärtigen Entwicklung der biologischen Schädlingsbekämpfungsmethoden in Polen
Abstract: The currents of the development of biological control in Poland. Gradually, complex methods of forests protection have been introduced. The great role has been stressed on biological control among others on the protection of birds and colonization of ants. The application in greenhouses of mite Phytoseiulus persimilis becomes more and more important. Among the basical works a great importance is given to the research on viruses of caterpillars. Recently, three new species have been described and their pathogenicity has been investigated. With a particular interest the researches on the parasite nematodes have been developed. These are concentrated on the nematodes of the genus Neoaplectana and the Pristionchus uniformis. The pathogenicity of these nematodes has been investigated in relation to different insects, and also their pathogenicity jointly with the fungi of the genus Beauveria and Paecilomyces. The researches are based on original methods of the cultivation of the nematodes. It has also been taken into consideration the changes of ultra‐structure of the host's tissues and hemolimphe. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: E.F., Boller, Ernst F.; U., Remund, U.
Title: Erste Erfahrungen mit dem Selbstvernichtungsverfahren bei Rhagoletis cerasi L. in der Nordwestschweiz
Abstract: Preliminary conclusions concerning the application of the sterile insect technique against European cherry fruit fly (Rhagoletis cerasi L.) in Northwest Switzerland. Field experiments with sterile flies carried out in 1972 and 1973 are discussed. Whereas the 1972 experiments proved that the techniques involved and the logistic problems have reached a satisfactory level actual control (eradication) experiments started in 1973 and showed promising results. However, it is concluded that the success achieved (no infestations observed) was possible due to very favourable ecological conditions (low population densities of the pest) and that the method has to prove its feasibility also in more difficult situations. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: H.F., van Emden, Helmut Fritz
Title: Intra‐ und interspezifische Beziehungen: Ihre Wirkung auf die Populationsstabilität im Rahmen der Schädlingsbekämpfung
Abstract: Intra‐ and interspecific relationships: Their influence on population stability in the context of pest control. Ecological approaches to pest control are largely based on the theories of traditional population dynamics. Ecological energetics principles have received less attention, though they are more concerned with changes in ecosystems and therefore as, if not more, relevant to pest control than population dynamics. Diversity and stability do not appear to be causatively correlated; diversity merely creates a wide range of possibilities (the average of which tends to decreased stability) from which natural selection can select for stability. The evidence that, especially in immature ecosystems such as agroecosystems, diversity and stability are sometimes negatively correlated should not surprise us. The various control techniques included under the umbrella of pest management similarly represent a diversity of outcomes from which man, rather than natural selection, makes the choice. Many current pest control controversies are resolved if we examine them from three points of view: a. how do they effect energy flow? b. the position of the crop ecosystem in the plant succession, c. is the purpose of control of a particular pest to keep it at or hold it below its equilibrium population? 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: T., Kock, Theodor
Title: Abwehr von Schäden des Erdbeerlaufkäfers, Harpalus pubescens Müll. (Coleoptera, Carabidae), im Erdbeeranbau durch eine Ablenkfütterung
Abstract: Protection of strawberries against Harpalus pubescens (Col., Carabidae) by feeding the beetles with averting substances. The strawberry seed beetle Harpalus pubescens Müller is the most frequent carabid besides Pterostichus vulgaris and sometimes injures the strawberry plantations in the region of, Mittelbaden” very much. Experiments on its density and activity carried out in 1971–1973 had comparable results to the findings of Scherney 1959) for other cultural biotops. In feeding‐experiments it could be shown repeatedly that H. pubescens prefers a zoophagous habit. Therefore the change from a zoophagous to a phytophagous habit causing an increased population in the strawberry cultures (where the beetles eat up only the seeds of the berries), must have another reason than a sudden preference of fruit nutrition. The reason for the change of the nutrition habit seems to be the lack of an adequate animalic food for H. pubescens. This seems to be the consequence of the application of chemical control to insects and slugs. A chemical control to H. pubescens is not possible because of different reasons: Its appearance‐time is the flowering period and insecticides would be toxic to honey bees. The non‐toxic insecticides to honey bees have such a long withholding period, that they would cause residues in the fruit. Moreover nearby all natural enemies, the predaceous arthropods, are attacked by chemical control. Therefore, in field experiments during two years a method has been developed to avert the beetles from the strawberry cultures by feeding them with groats of soja beans. By this ”averting‐feeding„ it is possible to keep the damage to the strawberries within a tolerable extend. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: D.V., Dev, D. V.; U.R., Batra, Usha Rani; R.N., Joshi, Ramchandra N.
Author full names: Dev, D. V. (57214300270); Batra, Usha Rani (57152721300); Joshi, Ramchandra N. (16525199300)
Title: The yields of extracted leaf protein from lucerne (Medicago sativa L.)
Source title: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
Abstract: The effects of fertilisers, frequency of cutting, row spacing and simazine on the yields of dry matter and extractable protein from lucerne (Medicago sativa L.) were studied using the laboratory‐scale pulper and press. Between 40 and 65% protein nitrogen was extractable; extractability was not affected by the various treatments but altered with season. Lucerne responded with increased yields of dry matter and extractable protein to fertilisers, simazine (35 g/ha) and rows spaced at 30.5 cm. Six or 8 harvests were found to give greater yields than 5 harvests in 180 days. The annual yields of extractable protein reached 3100 kg/ha and it is felt that better control of pests could lead to even greater yields. Authors: W.D., Englert, W. D.
Title: Revision der Gattung Metzneria Zeller (Lepid., Gelechiidae) mit Beiträgen zur Biologie der Arten
Abstract: Revision of genus Metzneria Zeller (Lep., Gelechiidae) with contributions to the biology of species. Studies on biocontrol projects of weeds, carried out at the European Station of the Commonwealth Institute of Biological Control in Délemont, Switzerland, lead to a special interest in taxonomy and biology of the genus Metzneria Zeller 1839. Rearing methods and preparation methods of genitalia slides are described. With the exception of one species, which was introduced in North‐America, most Metzneria spp. are endemic in the Palearctic region. All species, the host‐plants of which are known, are seed‐feeders. Most of them are restricted to the Cynareae, especially the genus Centaurea. The genus Metzneria is revised and all literature about this group is critically reviewed. In this revision 27 species, 1 subspecies, 3 uncleared species are separated. Metzneria riadella, M. diffusella, M. staehelinella and M. subflavella are described as new species. 15 species are found to be new synonyma. The parts of the male and female genitalia are described and determination‐keys are given for both. Information on host‐plants, biology and distribution are given. Possibilities, that species of this genus are used as biocontrol agents against Centaurea species in North America are discussed. Projekte über die Möglichkeiten der biologischen Bekämpfung von Unkräutern an der Europäischen Station des Commonwealth Institute of Biological Control in Delémont, Schweiz, führten zu einer näheren taxonomischen und biologischen Untersuchung der Gattung Metzneria Zeller 1839. Zunächst werden die Zuchtmethoden und die Herstellung von Genitalpräparaten be‐chrieben. Sodann werden die Systematik und Verbreitung der Gattung erörtert. Die Gattung kommt vorwiegend in der Westpaläarktis vor, eine Art wurde nach Nordamerika eingeschleppt. Die Grundzüge der Biologie der Arten werden umrissen. Die Wirtspflanzen der Metzneria‐Arten. gehören mit einer Ausnahme zu den Compositen, innerhalb welcher die meisten Metznerien auf Cynareen, vor allem auf der Gattung Centaurea leben. Es wird eine Revision der Gattung Metzneria und anschließend eine Zusammenfassung alles bisher über die einzelnen Metzneria‐Arten Bekannten gegeben. Dabei werden 27 Arten, 1 Unterart und 3 ungeklärte Arten unterschieden. 4 Arten sind davon neu. In 15 Fällen werden neue Synonyma innerhalb der Gattung festgestellt. Von den imaginalen Merkmalen werden die Genitalarmaturen beschrieben und zur Grundlage der nach männlichen und weiblichen Genitalarmaturen getrennten Bestimmungs‐schlüssel gemacht. Synonyma, Morphologie, Flugzeit, Wirtspflanzen, Lebensweise und Verbreitung der 27 Arten werden behandelt. Abschließend wird die Möglichkeit der Verwendung von Metzneria‐Arten zur biologischen Unkrautbekämpfung kurz erörtert. Révision sur le genre Metzneria Zeller (Lep., Gelechiidae), avec contribution sur la biologie des espèces Des projets sur les possibilités de la lutte biologique contre les mauvaises herbes, à la station européenne du Commonwealth Institute of Biological Control à Delémont, Suisse, conduisirent à une examination taxonomique et biologique plus précise du genre Metzneria Zeller 1839. Les méthodes de culture et la fabrication des préparations génitales sont décrites dans la partie générale. Le genre apparaît le plus souvent dans l'ouest du Paläarktis, mais une espèce s'introduisit en Amérique du Nord. A une seule exception, les plantes‐hôtes du genre Metzneria appartiennent à la famille des Composées. La plupart des Metzneria vivent sur des Cynareae, et surtout sur l'espèce Centaurea. Une révision sur le genre Metzneria est donnée dans la partie spécialisée, ainsi qu'un résumé de tout ce que l'on connaît sur les différentes espèces de Metzneria. On a différencié 27 espèces, dont 4 sont nouvelles pour la science, 1 sous‐espèce, et 3 espèces obscures. Dans 15 cas, de nouveaux synonymes ont été constatés dans le genre Metzneria. Les parties génitales sont décrites. Un tableau de détermination basé sur la séparation des parties génitales masculines et féminines a été établi. Une liste sur les genres et leurs synonymes a été effectuée, ainsi que pour les espèces obscures, les espèces transposées dans un autre groupe, et enfin pour le nomina nuda. Puis les 27 espèces sont traitées. La possibilité de l'emploi des Metzneria dans la lutte biologique contre les mauvaises herbes est discutée dans la dernière partie. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: L.H.M., Blommers, Leo H.M.
Title: Preliminary studies on two predators (Acarina: Phytoseiidae) of the spider mite Tetranychus neocaledonicus André (Acarina: Tetranychidae)
Abstract: Two malagasian species of predator mites of the genus Amblyseius Berlese can be reared with the phytophagous spider mite T. neocaledonicus, exclusively Amblyseius masiaka originated from spider mite infested plants in Western Madagascar. Spider mites alone are sufficient food for this species. Though the webbing of the prey hinders A. masiaka to some degree, this species is promising as a biological control agent. A. vazimba was found only once in the region of Tuléar. Addition of bee honey to the spider mite diet improves the reproductivity of this species considerably. If only spider mites are available the predator mite shows a strong tendency to leave the rearing units. It is doubtful whether this species can be of use in biological mite control. Untersuchungen über zwei Raubmilben als Feinde von Tetranychus neocaledonicus André (Acarina: Tetranychidae) Zwei Raubmilben‐Arten der Gattung Amblyseius Berlese von Madagaskar konnten unter Darbietung der Spinnmilbe T. neocaledonicus als Nahrung aufgezogen werden. Amblyseius masiaka n. sp. lebt auf mit Spinnmilben besetzten Pflanzen in West‐Madagaskar. Ihr genügten T. neocaledonicus als Nahrung. Obwohl das Spinngewebe der Beutetiere sie mehr oder weniger belästigt, dürfte sie für die biologische Bekämpfung dieser Spinnmilben in Frage kommen. A. vazimba n. sp. ist bisher nur einmal im Gebiet von Tuléar gefunden worden. Die Zugabe von Bienenhonig zu ihrer Nahrung beschleunigt ihre Fortpflanzungs‐geschwindigkeit. Ihr scheint eine reine Ernährung mit Spinnmilben nicht zu bekommen. Es ist zweifelhaft, ob sie für die biologische Bekämpfung verwendet werden kann. 1974 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: R.R., Mishra, R. R.; V.B., Srivastava, V. B.
Title: Leaf surface microflora of Hordeum vulgare L.
Abstract: The fungal and bacterial population of leaf surface of Horde, L. has ben described. The phyllosphere and phylloplane regions of green and yellow leaves harboured different dominant species. liacteria mostly supprcsscd the fungal growth and possibility of biological control has been suggested. The effect of three amino acids and one organic acid on leaf mycoflora has been studied by foliar spray method. Stimulatory effect of different concentrat ons of the acids has been noticed. Preferential growth of selected forms of microorganisms may be encouraged by the acid application to act as a mean of biological control. © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: I.L., Riding, Irene L.; N.G.M., Hague, Nigel Graham Meckenzi
Author full names: Riding, Irene L. (23055462200); Hague, Nigel Graham Meckenzi (7004701757)
Title: Some observations on a Tylenchid nematode Howardula sp. parasitizing the mushroom phorid Megasalia halterata (Phoridae, Diptera)
Abstract: Howardula sp. parasitizes the Mushroom phorid fly Megasalia halterata destroying the fat body and follicular membrane of the fly, decreasing copulation and egg output. With increasing hyperinfestation the fly is rendered sterile. Howardula sp. is host density dependent and reaches a maximum incidence in September and October. Under laboratory conditions fly populations were eliminated in three to five generations. The implications for possible biological control of M. halterata are discussed. Authors: I.J., Wyatt, Ian J.; B., Gurney, Barbara
Title: The efficiency of spawning machines for mixing insecticides into mushroom compost
Abstract: Insecticides incorporated into mushroom compost, using a spawning machine, are seldom mixed uniformly enough to achieve satisfactory pest control. The mixing efficiencies of various application methods and machines were investigated by mapping the distributions of fluorescent granules and emulsions under ultraviolet light. The pattern in which granules were applied to a compost block greatly affected the distribution after mixing but even uniformly peppering the surface resulted in acceptable concentrations in only 49% of the compost. Mixing twice increased this to 57%. With three times as many smaller granules, 89% of the compost was acceptably treated. Watering or spraying the compost with emulsions gave poor distributions except when the spray was directed into the spinner, which acceptably treated 83%. A machine which threw compost upwards into a hood beyond the spinner before it fell into a tray, gave better mixtures than conventional machines. The granule distribution affected the control of Heteropeza pygmaea larvae. Virtually complete control was obtained by peppering diazinon granules on to compost at 50 ppm a.i. and then mixing twice through a spawning machine. Copyright © 1974, Wiley Blackwell. Authors: S., Hörstadius, Sven
Title: Linnaeus, animals and man
Source title: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society
Abstract: Linnaeus is often undervalued as a zoologist. His importance lies not only in the introduction of binomial nomenclature and his Systema Naturae. As a systematist he divided the insects into the groups, Coleoptera, Hemiptera, Lepidoptera, Neuroptera, Hymenoptera, Diptera and Aptera. His programme, as expressed in his Methodus in Systema Naturae (1st ed.) is astounding in its biological manysidedness. He was before his time in many respects: he wrote and lectured upon bird migration, biological control of insects with their parasites or predators, protective mimicry, the struggle by all organisms for survival, contagious diseases as well as fermentation due to small living particles. He was the first to call attention to the close relationship between man and the anthropoid apes. Copyright © 1974, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: D.S., Hill, D. S.
Title: Susceptibilities of Carrot Cultivars to Carrot Fly (Psila rosae (F.)
Abstract: In 1972 a trial on susceptibility to carrot fly infestation was conducted on peat soil in East Anglia using 17 carrot cultivars sown on two dates one month apart. The only insecticide applied to the carrots was an aphicidal spray. The early‐sown carrots were damaged by the first generation of larvae, but, by the second sampling date in October, there were no infestation differences between the two sowings. At harvest in December, significant differences in infestation levels occurred; these ranged from 82 per cent damaged roots for Amster‐dammer Bak, 87 and 88 for two stocks of Royal Chantenay, to 97 per cent for Danvers 126. It is not yet clear whether the differences can be profitably exploited as an adjunct to other methods for controlling this pest. Copyright © 1974, Wiley Blackwell. Authors: H.Z., Levinson, Hermann Z.
Title: Possibilities of Using Insectistatics and Pheromones in the Control of Stored Product Pests
Abstract: Salient aspects of insect cuticle formation, hormone action, nutritional requirements, feeding stimulants, sex and aggregation pheromones are discussed in the light of their possible contribution to controlling storage pests. Agents decimating pest populations by suppression of growth and reproduction (rather than by rapid mortality) are defined as insectistatics. Their mode of action includes inhibition of chitin and sclerotin formation, hormonal imbalance induced by extrinsic juvenoids or ecdysoids, developmental disturbances due to nutrient or metabolite antagonists, accelerators of metabolism and symbioticides. Disruption of mating may be accomplished by pheromone trapping and disorientation, or prevention of sex attraction due to pheromone isomers. The relatively limited space and constant conditions in storehouses (moderate levels of humidity, temperature and ultraviolet light) as well as the rapid developmental rate and low population density of storage pests render them suitable for control by insectistatics and pheromones. Some of the latter are currently tested under natural conditions. The limitations of these biotechnical procedures are discussed. Copyright © 1974, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: F.L., Watters, F. L.
Title: Impact of Research on Grain Storage Practices in Canada
Abstract: Cold winters, a well‐developed bulk handling system, regular inspections of elevator premises, stored grain and cargo ships, and the application of pest control measures when necessary, minimize storage problems in Canadian grain. Research has played an important role in identifying the organisms and circumstances which cause infestations of stored grain and in developing and evaluating environmental, physical and chemical methods for preventing and controlling infestations. This information enables commercial grain organizations and government regulatory agencies to provide high quality grain for domestic consumption and export markets. Copyright © 1974, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: G., Liotta, G.; G., Mineo, G.
Title: RESUME:Studies on the Chemical Control of Aonidiella aurantii (Mask.)
Abstract: Aonidiella aurantii (Mask.) which was accidentally introduced in Sicily in 1968 has since become a dangerous pest requesting special treatments in citrus groves. Experiments have been carried out on Citrus lemon to evaluate the efficacy of several organophosphorous compounds partly in mixture with white oil and this latter applied sole (cf. table 1). The results obtained against young females are set out in table 2; they show excellent results with almost all compounds whereas the same pesticides had a rather poor effect on mature females (cf. table 3). It is concluded that the replacement of white oils by organophosphorous compounds is not justified providing that the control is directed against larvae and young females. This means that a proper timing is essential to obtain a satisfactory mortality, thus avoiding the use of detrimental broad acting pesticides. Copyright © 1974, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: F., Ashman, F.; D.J., Webley, David J.; N.Z., Achillides, N. Z.
Author full names: Ashman, F. (6505817765); Webley, David J. (6602776801); Achillides, N. Z. (57190483170)
Title: Space Treatment of Warehouses Using Dichlorvos
Abstract: Details are given of the performance of Vapona Pest Strips and of an automatic dichlorvos sprayer developed to prevent infestation of clean or fumigated stored commodities, for infestation control on stored carobs. Air concentrations after spraying a nominal dose of 10 μg/1 of total store space averaged approximately 1.0. μ g/l after 30 minutes and less than 0.3 μ g/l after 3 hours. Residues found on carobs after daily spraying of stores at 10 μ g/1 for 96 days were in the range of 0.2 ‐ 2.0 ppm. Ephestia cautella Walk, and Lasioderma serricorne (F.) become established in carobs after harvest and are the principle pests causing damage during storage. Effective control of E. cautella was obtained by using Shell Vapona Pest Strips at two strips/100 m3 or by daily spraying of dichlorvos at 10g/1,000 m2 (10μ g/1). No effect was observed against migrating larvae of E. calidella (Guen.) or E. figulilella Greg, nor against Bracon hebetor Say., the hymenopterous parasite attacking all three Ephestia species. The automatic dichlorvos sprayer is equipped to apply a predetermined dose at time of peak flight activity, 18–20 hours each evening. On stored carobs, no spraying is needed after October because the commodity temperature falls below 200C, too low for active development of the pest species. 23 automatic sprayers are now used in Cyprus to protect the whole carob crop from storage pests. Copyright © 1974, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: L., Brader, L.
Title: Integrated Control in the Netherlands 1)
Abstract: In the Netherlands the need for an ecological approach in pest control has led to the establishment in 1958 of the Research Group on harmonious control of arthropod pests later renamed into Research Group on integrated control of arthropod pests which has several sections. This Group is part of the National Council for Agricultural Research of the Organization for Applied Scientific Research (TNO). There is a close co‐operation between many Research Institutes towards developing integrated control of which the TNO Research Group is the co‐ordinating body. The research priorities have been clearly defined and the ways leading to a practical implementation of integrated control studied. Copyright © 1974, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.A., Freeman, J. A.
Title: RESUME:Orientation de la recherche au Laboratoire de lutte contre les déprédateurs des produits stockés (Pest Infestation Control Laboratory) de Slough
