Title: Chemical Control of Some Squash Pests in U.A.R.
Abstract: Four experiments were carried out, to evaluate the effect of granules and emulsions on squash pests and to detect their effect on the percentages of germination and yield insecticides. In the first experiment, the seeds were treated, at planting time. Each of Temik and Thimet gave high percentage as well of germination as in controlling aphids and spider mites; Valexon and Kelthane, gave nonpromising results. In the second experiment the pesticides were applied by side dressing method with the fertilizer. All treatments outyielded the check but without significant differences and Temik plots were the highest in yield. Pesticides did not affect the percentage of the total soluble solids in fruits. In the third experiments, emulsions of Anthio, Folimat, Valexon, Perfekthion and Kelthane were tested. Folimat ranged first in controlling aphids, white flies, and spider mites; Valexon and Kelthane, gave nonpromising results. In the fourth experiment emulsions of Rogor, Valexon, Gusathion, Kelthane and Folimat were tested. Each of Rogor and Folimat gave the highest percent control of aphids, white flies, thrips and spider mites. Other treatments gave poor results. Generally the applying of Rogor and Folimat can be considered as a successful combined treatment of insect and mite pests on squash. Authors: A.F.H., Besemer, A. F.H.
Title: Some Aspects of Chemical Control of Soil‐borne Pathogens
Abstract: The effect of a soil fumigant on soil‐borne pests and pathogens depends largely on a sufficient distribution through the top soil and the availability of the fumigant or the biologically active degradation products in the water phase. Nearly all the fumigants are dispersed in the soil mainly in the vapour phase and therefore the amount of air between the soil particles is very important. Consequently on light soils it is relatively easy to obtain an efficient control, but on heavy or wet soils and on soil types with a high humus content it is rather difficult to get reliable results. The concentration of the fumigant in the upper few cm. of the soil is often insufficient to get good control after injection of the material at 15–20 cm. depth. The effect may be improved by using a plastic cover or a «split plot» application. The elimination of most of the fumigant, to avoid a phytotoxic effect is a cause for concern on wet soils and on soil types with a high organic content. Factors influencing the decrease of the fumigant residue in the soil are discussed. The soil fumigant application gives rise to important changes in the whole ecosystem in the soil. Information on the influence on non‐target organisms is scarce. The application of dichloropropene and of chloropicrin may lead to a noticeable effect on the nitrificating bacteria. The soil application of fumigants may give rise to residues in plants of the parent chemical or, to a larger extent, to residues of metabolites e.g. Br‐ after soil disinfection with Br‐ containing fumigants such as methylbromide, EDB1), etc. The enrichment of the soil with Br‐ may cause phytotoxic effects on susceptible crops such as carnations. The fate of the metabolites arising from dichloropropene and related compounds has not been fully clarified. Copyright © 1972, Wiley Blackwell. Title: Soil‐borne Pests and Pathogens Associated with Imported Plants, with Special Reference to Nematodes
Abstract: The assessment of phytosanitary risks from imported soil entails recovery or assay of soil‐borne organisms, determination of pathogenicity and consideration of potential distribution as affected by environmental factors. Results are presented of examinations of soil from imported plants for nematodes and other pests. Nematodes were much more abundant than other pest groups. Plant‐parasitic nematodes were more common in natural soils than in potting composts, and non‐indigenous species were apparently more frequent from non‐European than European sources. The chief nematode hazards for northern European countries may be from new «pathotypes» of Heterodera species and ectoparasitic dorylaimid genera that include virus vectors. Title: Pheromones of IPS pini (Coleoptera: Scolytidae): Variation in response among three populations
Abstract: Reciprocal field tests of attraction between populations of Ips pini (Say) from California, Idaho, and New York disclosed geographic variation in pheromone systems. These differences reside both in pheromone production and reception. However, it is unknown whether variation in the pheromone bouquets is qualitative, quantitative, or both. In New York, both sexes responded in higher numbers to their own pheromone than that produced by California or Idaho males. In California, beetles of both sexes discriminated against New York, but in Idaho only females made this distinction. In both California and Idaho, the local population showed a slight preference for the pheromone produced by Idaho males over that produced by California males. The predator Enoclerus lecontei (Wolc.) demonstrated a four-fold preference for attractants produced by males from New York over those produced by beetles from California and Idaho. The parasitoid Tomicobia tibialis Ashmead showed the opposite trend. There is no evidence that geographic variation in the pheromones produced by I, pini is sufficient to enforce breeding isolation between adjacent populations. However, these results dramatize the necessity of considering pheromonal variability in programs applying pheromones for the survey and control of widely distributed pests. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. Authors: H.E., Knopf, H. E.
Title: Forestentomological Studies in Iraq: II. The Pest Problem of Poplar Cultivation
Abstract: A number of abiotic and biotic factors indicates that poplars of the section Aigeiros cultivated in the Northern Lowlands of Iraq in irrigated plantations had to grow at or near their ecological pessimum. These conditions make them optimal hosts for their dangerous insect enemy Melanophila picta (Pall.) and other insects and pathogens, occuring on the native Populus euphratica in small numbers. Favoured by the hot climate from the point of view of this insects specific temperature requirements and by the fact that environmental factors for these poplars reach in Iraq the negative culmination and putting to degeneration that part of the tree which is needed by Melanophila picta larvae, just at that season and in that state, development and further spread is ensured also from the point of view of nutrition. This coincidence of factors which favours directly and indirectly that insect, leads consequently to outbreaks and is considered responsible for the complete destruction of the plantations, to which a number of other insects and pathogens mentioned in this paper, very probably might have contributed. Forstentomologische Studien im Irak. II. Das Schädlingsproblem beim Pappelanbau Eine Anzahl abiotischer und biotischer Faktoren weist darauf hin, daß Pappeln der Sektion Aigeiros, welche im nördlichen Flachland des Irak angebaut wurden, im oder in der Nähe des Bereichs ihres ökologischen Pessimums wachsen. Dieser Umstand machte sie zu optimalen Wirtspflanzen für den gefährlichen Pappelschädling Melanophila picta (Pall.) sowie andere Insekten und Krankheitserreger, welche an der einheimischen Populus euphratica in geringerer Zahl vorkommen. Melanophila picta wird einerseits hinsichtlich seiner spezifischen Temperaturanforderungen vom heißen Klima im Irak begünstigt, andererseits auch durch ein optimales Nahrungsangebot, da die Umweltfaktoren gerade zu dieser Jahreszeit einen Höhepunkt der Ungunst erreichen und jene Teile der Bäume physiologischer Degeneration aussetzen, welche die Melanophila‐Larven eben zu dieser Zeit und in diesem Zustand als Nahrung benötigen. Dieses Zusammentreffen von Faktoren, die direkt sowie indirekt den Schädling stark begünstigen, wird als Ursache für die Massenvermehrung und die völlige Vernichtung der Pappelplantagen angesehen, zu der auch eine Reihe von anderen Insekten und Krankheitserregern, die in dieser Arbeit erwähnt sind, beigetragen haben mögen. 1972 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: K.P., Carl, Klaus P.
Title: On the Biology, Ecology and Population Dynamics of Caliroa cerasi (L.) (Hym., Tenthredinidae)
Abstract: This paper describes the taxonomy, geographical distribution, biology, phenology and voltinism, diapause, ecology and population dynamics of C. cerasi. In Europe, the pear‐slug is a pest of secondary importance with cherry as principal host plant. Outbreaks occur at irregular intervals. In the beginning of an outbreak in the Alsace the species was mainly bivoltine, with a small univoltine intermediate generation, but there occurred a gradual shift in the course of the gradation towards a predominance of the intermediate generation, and also a shift from deuterotokous to thelytokous parthenogenesis. Climate and weather could not be shown to have a marked effect on the population dynamics of C. cerasi. Larval and cocoon parasitism were often important mortality factors and are considered as an efficient regulating mechanism, whilst egg parasitism was unimportant. There are indications that other, most likely intrinsic factors also contribute to the break‐down of outbreaks, because a high mortality due to unknown causes was observed in the larval and eonymphal stages in the retrogradation phase of an outbreak. Zur Biologie, ökologie und Populationsdynamik von Caliroa cerasi (L.) (Hym., Tenthredinidae) Die Arbeit gibt eine zusammenfassende Darstellung der taxonomischen Stellung, geographischen Verbreitung, Biologie, Phänologie, Diapause, ökologie und Populationsdynamik der Kirschenblattwespe. Die Generationsfolge von C. cerasi wird dadurch kompliziert, daß zu den normalen zwei Generationen eine univoltine Intermediärgeneration hinzukommt. Die Zyklen sind nicht streng voneinander getrennt, d. h. sowohl aus der bivoltinen Population gehen Tiere in die Intermediärgeneration über als auch umgekehrt. Im Verlaufe einer Massenvermehrung im Elsaß wurde ein ständiges Anwachsen der Intermediärgeneration und ein entsprechender Rückgang der bivoltinen Population festgestellt. In Mitteleuropa ist C. cerasi teil deuterotok, teils thelytok parthenogenetisch. Am Anfang der Gradation im Elsaß wurden 1961 27% Männchen beobachtet; der Anteil der Weibchen nahm dann ständig zu, bis am Ende der Retrogradation 1966 die Population rein thelytok war. Experimentell konnte nachgewiesen werden, daß Kurztag die Diapause induziert, in der das Insekt als Eonymphe überwintert. Junglarven reagieren empfindlicher auf Kurztag als Altlarven, und mindestens drei Larvenstadien müssen ihm ausgesetzt werden, damit die Diapause ausgelöst wird. Umgekehrt kann sie vollständig unterdrückt werden, wenn sich sechs Larvenstadien bei Langtag entwickeln. Hohe Temperatur in Verbindung mit Kurztag verhindert die Diapause nicht. Damit wird sichergestellt, daß auch bei hohen Freilandtemperaturen die Intermediär‐ und Herbstgeneration Diapause‐Eonymphen ausbilden. Dagegen vermindert tiefe Temperatur die Wirkung von Langtag. Daraus erklärt sich, daß, in Abhängigkeit von den Temperaturverhältnissen im Freiland, ein wechselnder Anteil von Larven der ersten Generation Diapause‐Eonymphen ergibt. — Ein Brechen der einmal induzierten Diapause gelang nicht. Lagerung von Eonymphen bei + 8° C und bei — 12° C hatte keinen, bei + 3° C hatte sie eine geringe beschleunigende Wirkung auf den Ablauf der Diapause. Als Schädling ist die Kirschenblattwespe in Europa von untergeordneter Bedeutung, da sie im Intensiv‐Obstbau wegen ihrer großen Empfindlichkeit gegen Insektizide schon durch Bekämpfungsmaßnahmen gegen andere Schädlinge (z. B. die Kirschenfliege) an Massenvermehrungen gehindert wird, weshalb Gradationen nur in vernachlässigten Beständen vorkommen. Außerdem treten Schäden an der am häufigsten befallenen Wirtspflanze, der Kirsche, in Mitteleuropa erst nach der Ernte auf. Ausnahmen bilden selten vorkommende Gradationen in Baumschulen; dort kann eine direkte Bekämpfung erforderlich werden. Die Ursachen von Massenvermehrungen, die in unregelmäßigen Zeitabständen auftreten, sind unbekannt. Wegen der außerordentlichen Ortsstetigkeit der Imagines ist der Befall einzelner Bäume in einem Gradationsgebiet sehr unterschiedlich. Die Gradation derart isolierter Populationen auf Einzelbäumen ist in der Regel von kürzerer Dauer als die der Population im gesamten Befallsgebiet. Meist konzentriert sich der Befall auf den unteren, dem Wind abgewandten Kronenbereich. Klima und Wetter hatten keine oder nur geringe Wirkung auf die Populationsdynamik von C. cerasi. Ohne Bedeutung waren Eiparasiten (Trichogramma sp.), dagegen bewirkten Parasiten von Larven und Eonymphen oft eine hohe Wirtssterblichkeit und werden als wirksame Begrenzungsfaktoren betrachtet. Von den Larvenparasiten Perilissus luteolator Grav., Rhinotorus congruens Hlgr., Eridolius rufonotatus Hlgr., Synomelix sp. und Vibrissina turrita Meig. waren die beiden erstgenannten am wirkungsvollsten mit hoher Konstanz und Abundanz. E. rufonotatus wurde nur bei Wien, V. turrita nur im schweizerischen Mittelland und im Elsaß in geringer Zahl gefunden. Synomelix sp. war zwar eine sehr konstante Art, aber trotz hoher Parasitierungswerte (bis über 90%) war sie von untergeordneter Bedeutung wegen einer außerordentlich hohen Einkapselungsrate der Parasiteneier und ‐larven im Wirt. Von den Kokonparasiten Aptesis abdominator Grav., A. nigrocinctus Grav. und Cleptes nitidulus Fabr. zeichneten sich besonders die beiden letztgenannten durch hohe Konstanz und Abundanz aus. A. abdominator ist ein Hauptparasit von Operophthera brumata L., und C. cerasi wird sicher nur zufällig angenommen. Im Elsaß und bei Waldshut im oberen Rheintal wurde gegen Ende der Gradation eine hohe Larven‐ und Eonymphensterblichkeit durch Vertrocknen der Tiere beobachtet, ohne daß dafür die Ursache bestimmt werden konnte. Eine Krankheit war nicht feststellbar, und es läßt sich nur spekulieren, daß möglicherweise ein “physiologisches Altern” der Population im Verlauf der Gradation oder verringerte Lebensfähigkeit infolge andauernder Thelytokie die Ursache war. Es ist jedoch sicher, daß dieses Phänomen neben der hohen Parasitierung am Zusammenbruch beider Massenvermehrungen wesentlich beteiligt war. 1972 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A.M., Abdel-Salam, Atef M.; A.M., Assem, A. M.; K.H., Yousef, K. H.
Title: Studies on Potato Pests in U.A.R. III. Effect of Some Insecticides on the Potato Tuber Worm in the Field and Storage
Abstract: Three experiments were conducted to evaluate some insecticides in controlling potato tuber worm in the field and storage. It was found that dusting the tubers in storage with Malathion 1% or Sevin 10% dust at the rate of one kg per ton of tubers protected the potato tubers from the attack of Phthorimaea operculella in storage while in the field Sevin 85% wp at the concentration of 0.4% and Guthion at the rate of 0.2% were the most effective insecticides against this insect pest. Studien über Kartoffelschädlinge in der V.A.R. III. Wirkung einiger Insektizide auf die Kartoffelmotte im Freiland und Lager Es wurden 3 Experimente durchgeführt, um die Wirkung einiger Insektizide auf die Raupen der Kartoffelmotte Phthorimaea operculella (Zell.) im Freiland und Lager zu prüfen. Eine Bestäubung der Kartoffel mit Malathion 1% oder Sevin 10% in einer Aufwandmenge von 1 kg/t Kartoffeln gewährte guten Schutz vor P. operculella‐Befall im Lager, während im Freiland Sevin 0,4% und Guthion 0,2% jeweils als Staub die besten Wirkungen zeigten. 1972 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Author full names: Maxwell, Fowden G. (16531560800); Jenkins, Johnie N. (57203812303); Parrott, William L. (7004520357)
Title: Resistance of plants to insects
Abstract: Examination of the literature pertaining to resistance to insects in plants reveals that there have been numerous outstanding successes in breeding for resistance. The value of these resistant crops cannot be fairly estimated except to say that it would range in the high millions of dollars annually. Second, the literature points out strikingly the great diversity within crop varieties and species screened for insect-resistant mechanisms. Only limited screening for a very restricted number of insects has been attempted, hence a virtual gold mine of potential for future exploitation lies before us. The increasing problems being encountered with insecticide resistance in insects, loss of insecticides by legislation, increasing concern of the general public over contamination of the environment are forces which will necessitate greater emphasis of this method of insect control. Even low levels of resistance to insects in crops will be extremely important as we combine cultural, biological, and selective factors into more sophisticated pest management systems for future insect control. Plant breeders, entomologists, plant pathologists, physiologists, and biochemists and workers in related disciplines have a great challenge before them to work effectively together in close, cooperative team efforts to provide the leadership, research competence, and impetus to move host plant resistance to insects to its full national and international potential. © 1972, Academic Press Inc. © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: C.P.F., de Lima, C. P.F.
Title: Lindane resistance in field strains of Sitophilus zeamais (Motsch.) in Kenya
Abstract: Forty field strains of Sitophilus zeamais were obtained from 23 locations in Kenya. After being cultured under standard laboratory conditions, their responses to lindane were compared with that of the Pest Infestation Control Laboratory standard susceptible strain by exposure to lindane impregnated papers. The susceptible strain showed some variation in response, its LC<inf>50</inf> ranging from 0·05 to 0·22 per cent in five series of tests. Factors of resistance in the field strains ranged from × 1 to × 49. In general strains with high resistance factors came from localities where lindane had been in regular use on stored maize. © 1972. © 2014 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: H.E., Daugherty, Howard E.
Title: Short communication
Abstract: Human influences have had a pronounced impact on the zoogeography of El Salvador. Several animal populations (particularly among the larger vertebrates) have been seriously depleted and some taxa have been exterminated. The principal causal agents have been habitat alteration and over-exploitation by Man. The ecological concomitants have been the simplification of ecosystems, a decrease in the animal protein base in the human diet, and an increase in the numbers of smaller rodents, many of which have become serious agricultural pests. © 1972. © 2014 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.A., Shemanchuk, Joseph A.
Title: Observations the abundance and activity of three species of ceratopogonidae (diptera) in northeastern alberta
Abstract: Three species of two genera in the family Ceratopogonidae, namely Culicoides obsoletus Meigen, Culicoides yukonensis Hoffman, and Dasyhelea sp. near tristyla Wirth were collected from the area near Fort McMurray, Alta. (lat. 5644’ N., long. 11 1°23’ W.). The order of abundance of the three species was C. obsoletus, C. yukonensis, and Dasyhelea sp. C. obsoletus and C. yukonensis were most active during the evening hours and Dasyhelea sp. was most active during daytime hours. Both species of Culicoides were serious pests of humans and animals in the community. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. All rights reserved. © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: G.K., Scheibelreiter, Georg K.
Title: Die Tenthrediniden der Rose (Rosa spec.)
Abstract: The Tenthredinoidea of Rosa spec. In connection with research on biological control measures against Rosa rubiginosa in New Zealand the Tenthredinids of Rosa spec. were studied in Austria by the Commonwealth Inst. of Biol. Control (CIBC), European Station, Delémont. 23 species were collected, belonging to the families of Tenthredinidae (15), Argidae (4), Pamphilidae (2) and Cephidae (2). In Part I distribution and abundance of the species as well as their preference of biotops are described. Keys of egg‐depots and of larval characteristics are given. Part II deals with the most important dates of bionomy of the 23 Tenthredinids. Many of these dates are based on own new observations. Im Zuge einer geplanten biologischen Bekämpfung von Rosa rubiginosa in Neu‐Seeland wurde vom Commonwealth Institute of Biological Control (CIBC), European Station, an der Austrian Substation in Neulengbach der Tenthredinidenkomplex von Rosa spp. untersucht. Das Hauptuntersuchungsgebiet lag in Ostösterreich. Insgesamt wurden 23 Blattwespen‐Arten gesammelt, die sich auf die Familien der Tenthredinidae (15), Argidae (4), Pamphilidae (2) und Cephidae (2) verteilen. Im allgemeinen Teil der Arbeit werden die Biotopbindung, geographische Verbreitung und Häufigkeit der Arten behandelt und Gelege‐ sowie Larvenbestimmungsschlüssel aufgestellt. Im speziellen Teil wird das über die Lebens‐ u. Schadensweise der gefundenen 23 Blattwespenarten Bekannte kurz zusammengestellt. Authors: A.M., Abdel-Salam, Atef M.; M.A., Assem, M. A.; S.M., Hammad, S. M.; G.H., Eid, G. H.
Title: Studies on Potato Pests in U. A. R. II. Susceptibility of Some Potato Varieties to Insect Infestation in the Field and in the Storage
Abstract: Four experiments were carried out in the field and in the storage to study the susceptibility of 12 potato varieties to insects infestation, potato tuber worm Phthorimaea operculella Zell., tomato white fly Bemisia tabaci Genn., potato leafhopper Empoasca fabae Harris, onion thrips, Thrips tabaci Lind., and green peach aphid Myzus persicae Sulzer. Claudia variety ‐was the least susceptible to potato tuber worm infestation followed by Alpha A. Seinge was the more susceptible variety. There were no significant differences between the tested varieties in the degree of infestation by white fly. Alpha A; Alpha E, Alpha B, Claudia and Seinge were less susceptible to the potato leaf hopper infestation while Perviosnic and King Edward were the more susceptible varieties. Alpha A and Seinge were significantly less susceptible to the green peach aphid wihle Gevont and Aran Banner were more susceptible. The three Alpha varieties proved to be the less susceptible varieties to onion thrips infestation, while Perviosnic, King Edward and Patrones were the most susceptible varieties. Empfindlichkeit einiger Kartoffelsorten gegen Insektenbefall im Feld und auf dem Speicher Es wurden 4 Untersuchungen an Freiland‐ und gelagerten Kartoffeln über die Empfindlichkeit von 12 Kartoffelsorten gegenüber dem Befall durch die Kartoffelmotte (Phthorimaea operculella Zeller), die Tomatenmotten‐Schildlaus (Bemisia tabaci Genn.), den Kartoffelblattfloh (Empoasca fabae Harris), den Tabakthrips (Thrips tabaci Lind.) und die grüne Pfirsichlaus (Myzus persicae Sulzer) durchgeführt. Gegen die Kartoffelmotte war die Varietät Claudia am wenigsten, die Varietät Seinge am stärksten empfindlich. Bei Bemisia tabaci waren keine gesicherten Befallsunterschiede zu erkennen. Alpha A, E und B sowie Claudia und Seinge erwiesen sich am wenigsten, Perviosnic und King Edward am stärksten anfällig gegen den Kartoffelblattfloh. Alpha A und Seinge waren signifikant weniger anfällig gegen die grüne Blattlaus als die Varietäten Gevont und Aran Banner. Die 3 Alpha‐Varietäten zeigten gegenüber Thrips tabaci die geringste, Perviosnic, King Edward und Patrones die höchste Empfindlichkeit. 1972 Blackwell Verlag GmbH © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: S.I., El-Sherif, S. I.; S.M., Hammad, S. M.; S.K., El-Sawaf, S. K.
Title: Field Observations on Leucania loreyi (Dup.) (Lepid., Noctuidae) in Egypt
Abstract: Under field conditions, only maize and sugar‐cane plants are susceptible to Leucania loreyi. Detailed descriptions of the pest's symptoms of infestation, and the behaviouristics of its different stages on both crops are given. However, laboratory trials indicated the validity of rice, wheat, barley and broomcorn leaf‐blades for rearing larvae. In field experiments, female moths expressed a definite oviposition preference for maize plants, while they entirely rejected those of sugar‐cane. Under field conditions the 1st instar larvae persisted on maize plants only and never attacked sugar‐cane, but those of the 4th instar invaded both plants with a marked preference for maize. Regardless of host plant, larvae showed a noticable preference to older plants. Population fluctuation, as measured by adult catches in a U.V. light trap operated for about two years in Alexandria area, indicated that two main periods of abundance are of common occurrence. The first abundance takes place from March to June, and is evidently stronger than the second, which occupies October and November. Freilanduntersuchungen über Leucania loreyi (Dup.) (Lep., Noct.) in Ägypten Unter Freilandverhältnissen waren nur Mais und Zuckerrohr durch L. loreyi gefährdet. Es wird eine detaillierte Beschreibung der Befallszeichen sowie der Verhaltensweise der Entwicklungsstadien des Schädlings an beiden Pflanzenarten gegeben. Laborzuchten erwiesen die Eignung auch von Reis‐, Weizen‐, Gerste‐ und Broomkornblättern zur Aufzucht der Larven. Im Freiland zeigten die ♀♀ Falter eine ausgeprägte Eiablagepräferenz für Maispflanzen, während sie Zuckerrohr völlig ablehnten. Unter Freilandbedingungen blieben die Erstraupen am Mais und suchten nicht danebenstehende Zuckerrohrpflanzen auf. Jedoch fraßen die Viertraupen an beiden Pflanzenarten, unter Bevorzugung von Mais. Unabhängig von der Wirtspflanzenart zeigten die Raupen eine deutliche Vorliebe für ältere Pflanzen. 2jährige Registrierungen der Populationsfluktuation mit Hilfe von UV‐Lichtfallen ergaben 2 Hauptperioden des Auftretens. Title: Mosquitoes of manitoba III. Ecology of larvae in the winnipeg area
Abstract: Larval surveys were conducted in Winnipeg environs during the summers of 1967 and 1968. The species, density of larvae, the relationship between rainfall and larval abundance, and the species of pest importance were studied in detail. Aedes vexans was the most numerous mosquito found both in the larval and adult stages. Aedrs dorsalis and Aedes sprr~cerii were also of pest significance during each season. An association between the abundance of A. vexar~s larvae and the proximity of these to an adult blood source, mainly beef and dairy cattle, was observed. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. Authors: A.M., Smith, Alan M.
Title: Nutrient leakage promotes biological control of dried sclerotia of Sclerotium rolfsii Sacc
Abstract: Dried sclerotia of Sclerotium rolfsii Sacc. rapidly rot in moist soil because they leak nutrients. The nutrients are an energy source for microorganisms in the vicinity of the sclerotia, giving them sufficient colonization potential to breach the defence mechanisms of the sclerotia. Drying the sclerotia also stimulates their germination in soil but further research is needed before the mechanism can be described. Dried sclerotia washed in water until all nutrient leakage is removed still germinate in soil but do not rot. © 1972. © 2014 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.A., McFarlane, J. A.; P., Dobie, Philip
Title: The susceptibility of t'ef (Eragrostis abyssinica Schard.) to infestation by some insect pests of stored grain
Abstract: Insect-rearing experiments at 27°C and 70% r.h. on t'ef (the grain of Eragrostis abyssinica Schard.) showed that whole t'ef is unlikely to be infested by Sitophilus oryzae (L.) Rhyzopertha dominica (F.) or Sitotroga cerealella (Oliv.). Tribolium castaneum (Herbst) was the only insect, of eight species tested, able to multiply effectively on undamaged whole t'ef where it fed predominantly upon the grain embryo. T. destructor Uyttenb. and Ephestia cautella (Wlk.) showed some ability to produce surviving progeny on whole t'ef but are unlikely to be serious pests. Cryptolestes pusillus (Schon.) was able to infest t'ef in the presence of the other insect species and also multiplied effectively on milled t'ef, which suggests that it is the nature of the intact seed that prevents infestation in the absence of T. castaneum. It is likely that other insects with free-living larvae, including Oryzaephilus surinamensis (L.) which did not multiply on whole t'ef in these experiments, may be able to infest milled or damaged t'ef. However, none of the other species tested produced surviving larvae in the presence of T. castaneum (on whole t'ef). All eight species produced surviving progeny on whole wheat in separate cultures but in composite cultures O. surinamensis, E. cautella and S. cerealella were eliminated. © 1972. © 2014 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: F.T., Lord, F. T.
Title: Compaiusons of the abundance of the species composing the foliage inhabiting fauna of apple trees
Abstract: A 5 year study of the foliage inhabiting fauna of young apple trees which had never been treated with insecticides or miticides showed there were large numbers of species varying considerably in quantity. The study also showed that the manner in which the foliage is distributed by cluster type and the distribution of the many species on the clusters are important factors in the sampling of mixed populations of arthropods. The leaf clusters were classified into six types based on stem length and on the presence or absence of fruit. The mean number of leaves per cluster for all types combined increased until mid July but no further increase occurred after that. The variation in leaves per cluster on the longer clusters, however, continued throughout the summer even though the mean number of leaves per cluster did not. The relative abundance of each of the arthropod species, whether it was identifiable to name or not, was given a quantitative rating by using random clusters as a common sampling unit. Eleven orders, 38 families, and over 100 species were recorded. The species making up the fauna were nearly all at a low density and in general remained low during the study. All the common pests were found but only four were at a level where economic damage to the foliage resulted. Very few of the species were present in numbers sufficiently large for analysis of the factors iduencing their population density or their distribution. A list is given of those species which were sufficiently abundant to show that differences in preference for some cluster types over others is common. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. Authors: H.G., Wylie, H. G.
Title: Larval competition among three hymenopterous parasite species on multiparasitized housefly (Diptera) pupae
Abstract: Only one parasite species survived on most housefly (Musca domestica L.) pupae multiparasitized by any two of Nasonia vitripennis (Walk.), Muscidifurax zarapfor K. & L., or Spalangia cameroni Perk. N. vitripennis and M. zaraptor were both intrinsically superior to S. cameroni if the attacks on the hosts by their females preceded, were simultaneous with, or followed by up to 48 hours those by females of S. camerorri. N. vitriperlnis was intrinsically superior to M. zaraptor if its attack preceded that by M. zarapfor by at least 24 hours; M. zaraptor survived when it oviposited before N. vitriperznis; and neither species was consistently superior to the other when their attacks were simultaneous or that by N. vitriperltris closely preceded that by M. zaraptor-. N. vitripennis often survived on multiparasitized hosts because of its rapid development and rapid and thorough host utilization which caused its rivals to starve. In contrast, M. zarapfor's success was a consequence of its predation on eggs and larvae of its competitors and to a lesser extent its moderately rapid development and host utilization. S. camerorli was usually intrinsically inferior to both of the other species because, in spite of being predaceous on their larvae, it developed much more slowly and seldom attacked their eggs. The significance of these qualitative characteristics in insect parasites used in biological control programmes is discussed. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. Title: Aphidius platensis brethes, its distribution and host range (hym.: Aphidiidae)
Abstract: The research on the distribution and host range of Aphidius platensis has shown that this species is apparently indigenous to India, being further distributed in Africa, Australia, Middle East, South America, and Nearctic America (California-introduced). Authors: R.F., Morris, R. F.
Title: Predation by insects and spiders inhabiting colonial webs of hyphantrza cunea
Abstract: The number of predators inhabiting nests of Hyphatltria cunea Drury was recorded annually for 13 years in four areas in New Brunswick and two areas on the coast of Nova Scotia. The most common groups were the pentatomids and spiders, which sometünes reproduced within the nests, but the mean number per nest was low in relation to the number of H. cunea larvae in the colonies. The rate of predation on fifth-instar larvae was low. Small or timid predators appeared to prey 'largely on moribund larvae or small saprophagans during the principal defoliating instars of H. cunea. No relationship could be detected between the number of larvae reaching the fifth instar and the number of predators in the colony; nor could any functional or numerical response of the predators to either the initial number of larvae per colony or the population density of colonies be found. It is concluded that the influence of the nest-inhabiting predators is small and relatively stable, and may be treated as a constant in the development of models to explain the population dynamics of H. curlea. H. curlea is a pest in parts of Europe and Asia, where it has been accidentally introduced from North America. The introduction to other continents of the North American predator, Podisus maculiventris (Say), is discussed briefly. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. Authors: J.W., Osborn, J. W.
Title: On the biological improbability of Zahnreihen as embryological units
Abstract: An algebraic model is constructed to describe the ontogeny of the wave replacement of alternate teeth in lower vertebrates. It is pointed out that this model can be constructed in 2 ways, either by conforming to the biological controls inferred by the Zahnreihe theory of Edmund (1960, 1962) or to the biological inhibitions postulated by Osborn (1971) following a study of the ontogeny of the dentition of L. vivipara. It is argued that the latter theory incorporates biological possibilities and an economy of speculation which far outweigh the number and improbability of the speculations inferred by the Zahnreihe theory. It is noted that both the rate of tooth replacement in a tooth position and the rate of addition of tooth families at the back of the dentition are probably exponentially determined whereas the model constructed here, like that used to construct the Zahnreihe theory, is based on arithmetic progressions. © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M., Beroza, Morton
Title: Insect sex attractant pheromones, a tool for reducing insecticide contamination in the environment
Abstract: The major goals in studying sex attractant pheromones have been to upgrade efforts to combat insect pests and to diminish the disruptive effects of insecticides on the environment. A number of these pheromones have recently become available. They have been invaluable in detecting infestations of insect pests and in guiding control or eradication measures to prevent their spread. Some of the attractants may even be potent enough for use in direct control, e.g. in traps or in the 'confusion' technique. Sex attractant pheromones also have potential in integrated control programs; e.g. to time spray applications or combine with insecticides to make insecticide applications more efficient and more selective in their attack. Further study of sex pheromones, secondary chemicals, and volatility regulators will be needed to achieve full effectiveness of the sex attractants, and the technology of their use will have to be developed and tested in large scale field trials. Insect sex attractant pheromones are not a panacea, but they do have a place in pest control operations of the future, and they can be expected to alleviate some of the ecological problems associated with insect control. © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: S., Hasan, S.; C., Vago, Constantin
Title: The pathogenicity of Fusarium oxysporum to mosquito larvae
Abstract: Fusarium oxysporum was isolated from diseased larvae of the mosquito Aedes detritus collected in the marshy areas of Camargue, Southern France. The larvae of A. detritus and Culex pipeins pipiens were infected experimentally by contaminating water with conidia obtained from fungal cultures as well as by diseased cadavers. More than 80% mortality was obtained in the laboratory. Injured and young larvae demonstrated increased susceptibility to fungal infection. Histological preparations showed that spores germinating in the intestinal lumen were able to cause infection and the mycelium thus produced infected all tissues. Current experiments have shown that the fungus remains active even in greater quantities of water. Thus the disease may be considered as a possible limiting factor for mosquito populations, and eventually its use in biological control of mosquitoes merits further investigation. © 1973. © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Experimental infection of mosquito larvae by a species of the aquatic fungus Lagenidium
Abstract: A species of Lagenidium, an aquatic fungus isolated into pure culture from a living mosquito larva, has been shown to be a virulent parasite of Culex restuans. In laboratory experiments the level of infection in larval populations varied with the amount of inoculum which was supplied as zoospores. Over 90% of 4-day-old larvae subjected to 3 units of inoculum (ca. 0.5 million zoospores) were killed within 72 hr, whereas 10-day-old larvae with the same quantity of inoculum were stricken only at a 5% level. However, with 9 units of inoculum, over 80% of larvae at all ages tested up to 10 days were killed. It was noted also that when the host population was doubled. larval mortality was three times that of the control when 3 or 6 units of inoculum were utilized. High levels of mortality prevailed in all tests, regardless of host density or age, when 9 units of inoculum were applied. This fungus has been found to be effective also against other species of culicine mosquitoes, and its potential as an agent for the biological control of certain mosquitoes appears promising. © 1973. © 2014 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: W.T., Keane, William T.
Title: Eliminate DDT? Quest for an advantageous benefit:Risk ratio
Abstract: A review is made of some of the scientific and administrative procedures which have been suggested as possible methods of eliminating persistent economic poisons, such as DDT, from the environment. Even though the scientific techniques do not appear to hold much hope for the immediate future, the administrative procedures provided in the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act are presently being employed. This federal statute grants a significant degree of discretion to the Administrator responsible for regulating the flow of pesticides in interstate commerce. Prior to taking any action which might restrict or inhibit this flow, the Administrator is required to balance the beneficial effects resulting from the continued use of these products against the associated risks. Thus, the Administrator is constantly striving to achieve an advantageous benefit: risk ratio. Such a ratio can only be achieved if the Administrator judiciously employs the administrative discretion permitted under existing legislation. © 1972. © 2015 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: P.G., Fontana, P. G.
Title: Larvae of Dichetophora biroi (Kertesz, 1901) (Diptera: Sciomyzidae) feeding on Lymnaea tomentosa (Pfeiffer, 1855) snails infected with Fasciola hepatica L.
Abstract: It has now been clearly demonstrated that larval stages of the marsh flies belonging to the family Sciomyzidae (Diptera: Acalyptratae) feed exclusively on a wide range of aquatic and terrestrial gastropods (Berg, 1953, 1964; Knutson & Berg, 1963, 1967; Bratt, Knutson, Foote & Berg, 1969). Almost immediately after Berg's discovery (Berg, 1953) that the malacophagous habit is a general characteristic of the larval stages of the family Sciomyzidae as a whole, the question was raised as to whether these flies could be effectively employed in the biological control of snail-borne diseases, such as fascioliasis and schistosomiasis. Attempts have been made in Hawaii, Guam and Australia to control the intermediate hosts of Fasciola gigantica and F. hepatica with a number of sciomyzid species (Chock, Davies & Chong, 1961; Lynch, 1962; Boray, 1969), but so far the results have been equivocal (Berg, 1964; Lynch, 1965; Boray, 1969). In areas where snail-borne diseases are endemic the question also arises as to whether sciomyzid larvae will attack indiscriminately infected and uninfected snails. It is not known, for example, whether sciomyzid larvae “recognize’ and reject infected snails or whether these snails become more vulnerable after being attacked by the predators. In fact, the defence mechanisms of the infected snails may well be impaired by the infection. The present work was undertaken to provide some quantitative information on these two distinct possibilities since they may have important practical implications. Dichetophora biroi (Kertesz) was chosen because it is the most widespread and abundant species of sciomyzid fly in Victoria. It occurs also in other areas of south-eastern Australia where Lymnaea tomentosa (Pfeiffer), the intermediate host of F. hepatica in Australia (Boray & McMichael, 1961), is endemic. D. biroi has been found to play a role in the dynamics of a discrete geographic population of L. tomentosa in South Australia (Lynch, 1965). © 1972, Cambridge University Press. Title: Effects of volatile substances released by foliage of Abies balsamea
Abstract: The principal substances released by the foliage of Abies balsamea (pinene α and β, limonene, phellandrene, fenchone, and thujone) were tested on a few entomopathogenic species of Bacillus "cereus group" and on several common bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas sp., and Staphylococcus sp. Authors: D.L., Jaquette, David L.
Title: A discrete time population control model
Abstract: A discrete time stochastic model is assumed to describe the growth behavior of a natural animal, pest, or even epidemic population. Periodically, control action representing, for example, harvesting or exterminating can be taken to modify the future growth of the population. Dynamic programming can be used to generate optimal control policies for models where growth and control produce economically measurable benefit or cost. This paper uses dynamic programming to find conditions under which the classically simple "single critical number policy" is optimal. These conditions are then expanded to include a wide range of control models and the optimal policy obtained is characterized as a "single critical function policy.". © 1972. © 2014 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: C.R., Maclellan, C. R.
Title: Codling moth populations under natural, integrated, and chemical control on apple in nova scotia (Lepidoptera: Olethreutidae)
Abstract: Codling moth populations on natural apple fruit trees scattered throughout Nova Scotia are compared with those in commercial orchards. In natural fruit, failure of crop, crop size, degree of isolation, amount of crowding by native trees, and natural enemies determine the level of codling moth numbers. Young commercial orchards require artificial control measures within a few years of first bearing fruit to prevent severe crop losses. In older commercial orchards natural controls require an occasional assist by chemical treatment to contain the codling moth below economically tolerable levels. Such treatment is applied to interfere as little as possible with known natural controls. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. All rights reserved. © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: The Ecological Approach to the Management of the Citrus Rust Mite Phyllocoptruta oleivorus (Ashm.)
Abstract: Ecological studies on the citrus rust mite P. oleivorus infesting citrus orchards at the northern coast of the Mediterranean Sea in the U.A.R. and its management were carried out for two years. Population behaviour of the pest was influenced by the prevailing climatic conditions and host preference, while the rôle of the predacious mites was not considerable there. Authors: A.M., Smith, Alan M.
Title: Drying and wetting sclerotia promotes biological control of Sclerotium rolfsii Sacc
Abstract: Drying the sclerotia of Sclerotium rolfsii Sacc, for short periods limits their survival in moist soil. The dried sclerotia are colonized by other micro-organisms and rot within 2 weeks in remoistened soil. This method of promoting microbial breakdown of sclerotia in soil in the absence of host plants has important practical implications in the biological control of S. rolfsii. Drying the sclerotia also stimulates their germination in moist soil in the absence of host plants or a suitable substrate. Germination, however, does not necessarily lead to breakdown of sclerotia nor is it a prerequisite for rotting. In nature, when host plants are present, drying may be the main mechanism for germination of sclerotia. This mechanism would explain adequately the haphazard incidence of disease caused by S. rolfsii even in uniformly infested soil. © 1972. © 2014 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: P., Harris, P.
Title: Food-plant groups of the semanophorinae (Lepidoptera: Sphingidae): A possible taxonomic tool
Abstract: The taxonomic framework of the lepidopterous family Sphingidae established by Rothschild and Jordan (1903) contains many anomalies. Indeed, it has been suggested that as the taxonomic lines run across both larval and host-plant groupings, the family should be totally rearranged. In this paper the host plants of the Semanophorinae (one subfamily of the Sphingidae) are examined and discussed. On the basis of host plants, five groups of sphingids, which appear to be taxonomic entities, are distinguished. The identification of the host-plant groups is also a preliminary to the use of Celerio euphorbiae (L.) for the biological control of weedy Euphorbia spp. in Canada. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. Authors: J., Kalmakoff, James; S.G., Moore, Syd G.; R.P., Pottinger, R. P.
Author full names: Kalmakoff, James (7004181999); Moore, Syd G. (7403536755); Pottinger, R. P. (56930438000)
Title: An iridescent virus from the grass grub Costelytra zealandica: Serological study
Abstract: Iridescent viruses have been isolated from Costelytra zealandica (CzIV) and from Wiseana cervinata (WIV), both New Zealand pasture pests. Serological comparisons of these viruses were made using precipitin end point and intragel cross-absorption tests in agar gels. CzIV was clearly serologically distinguishable from other iridescent viruses while WIV was closely related to Tipula iridescent virus (TIV), Sericesthis iridescent virus (SIV), and CzIV. © 1972. © 2014 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: W.J., Turnock, William J.
Title: Geographical and historical variability in population patterns and life systems of the larch sawfly hymenoptera : Tenthredinidae
Abstract: The larch sawfly, Pristiphora erichsonii (Hartig), has exhibited several distinctive population patterns in different parts of its Holarctic distribution and during different periods of time in some geographic areas. These patterns include a latent type, where the larch sawfly is never a pest, a permanent type, which causes severe damage, and several temporary types characterized by periodic outbreaks. The different population patterns are associated with differences in the life systems of the populations: the stable latent type with a diverse environment and a rich parasite complex; the stable permanent type with an impoverished parasite complex, interactions with food availability and no effective specific parasites; and the temporary type with an intermediate parasite complex which includes one very effective specific larval parasite. Thus, population stability is related to either maximal or minimal diversity in numbers of parasite species and instability to intermediate levels. The comparison of population patterns and life systems provides a guide to the development of biological control programs. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. Authors: L.M., Mckenzie, L. M.; B.P., Beirne, Bryan P.
Author full names: Mckenzie, L. M. (57189671157); Beirne, Bryan P. (6505805591)
Title: A grape leafhopper, erythroneura ziczac (homoptera: cicadellidae), and its mymarid (hymenoptera) egg-parasite in the okanagan valley, british columbia
Abstract: The leafhopper Erythrorleura ziczac Walsh is the most important insect on grape in the Okanagan Valley, B.C. Hairy-leaved varieties of grape are relatively resistant to attack. The leafhopper has two overlapping generations a year and overwinters in the adult stage. Its chief natural enemy is a mymarid egg-parasite, Anagrus epos Girault, which overwinters in the eggs of other species of leafhoppers on wild rose and apple so that intensity of parasitism of E. ziczac can be influenced by proximity of those plants to vineyards. © 1972, Entomological Society of Canada. All rights reserved. © 2016 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A.M., Smith, Alan M.
Title: Biological control of fungal sclerotia in soil
Abstract: Sclerotia of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (Lib.) de Bary, S. minor Jagger, and Sclerotium cepivorum Berk., dried for short periods then remoistened in soil, leak nutrients, are rapidly colonized by other microorganisms, and rot within 2-3 weeks. This treatment has important implications in the biological control of many soil-borne diseases caused by fungi that produce sclerotia. Drying also stimulated the germination of sclerotia of S. sclerotiorum and S. minor but not S. cepivorum. This study indicates that many of the conclusions in published work dealing with the germination and survival in soil of fungal sclerotia are invalid. This is because most researchers have used dried sclerotia without realizing that drying is an additional treatment and can bias results. © 1972. © 2014 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M.G., Day, M. G.; I.J., Linn, Ian J.
Title: Notes on the food of feral mink Mustela vison in England and Wales
Abstract: There is some apprehension about the possible effect of the introduced American mink Mustela vison upon the indigenous British fauna, either as a predator exerting new and excessive pressure upon native prey species, or as a carnivore competing for prey resources against native carnivores. Concern is also felt by preservers of game, and by keepers of small domestic animals (poultry and rabbits) about the mink's potential as a pest. To investigate the food habits of the mink in England and Wales the alimentary canals of 1165 trapped animals were examined, yielding 204 samples for analysis. The resulting information provides a general picture of the mink's diet, including seasonal variations. Comparisons were possible with similar work carried out in other countries, and with the diets of other British carnivores. Tentative conclusions were reached regarding the broad pattern of food relationships between the mink and other British animals, wild and domestic. Copyright © 1972, Wiley Blackwell.
